The dedupe key and any duplicate suppression.
The cross-tenant claim event with the supplied identifier.

title: Stage a bulk import that would bypass an approval
preconditions: Tenant acme. A 620-row file changes base pay for the sales organization.
The interactive path requires finance approval above a 5 percent increase.
94 rows exceed 5 percent.
story: As an HR business partner, I want a bulk path to run the same governance the interactive path runs, so that the batch is not a way round the approval
scenario: The file is staged and profiled against the declared schema. Validation runs every row against the same domain rules, authority and invariants the interactive path uses. Ninety-four rows exceed the finance approval threshold. They are not silently committed: they are excluded from the automatic set and routed for finance approval as their own bound children. The remaining 526 rows are simulated, approved on their aggregate effect, and committed as individual child intents with per-row outcomes.

acceptance_criteria.given: 94 rows would require finance approval interactively
acceptance_criteria.then: those rows are excluded from the automatic set and routed for approval; the batch is not a licence to skip governance

acceptance_criteria.given: the batch is simulated
acceptance_criteria.then: the approver sees the aggregate effect and the excluded set before approving

acceptance_criteria.given: some rows commit and others fail
acceptance_criteria.then: per-row outcomes are reported, each row carrying its own RequestState, and the batch reports no aggregate success claim and performs no false rollback

acceptance_criteria.given: the error rate exceeds the configured threshold
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused rather than committing the good rows silently

acceptance_criteria.given: the mapping is wrong and every row validates but means the wrong thing
acceptance_criteria.then: the aggregate effect is what the approver checks, and it is the last line of defence

data_read.dataops: staging area, mapping and prior imports
data_read.people: existing records the rows will change
data_read.compliance: authority for each row's change type

data_written.dataops: staging records, validation results and the batch record
data_written.compensation: committed changes as child intents

authorization_and_disclosure: The approver receives FULL disclosure of the aggregate and the excluded set; each affected worker receives FULL disclosure of their own change and notice.

failure_modes.condition: the excluded rows are committed with the rest
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the finance approval is bypassed at scale, which is the classic backdoor

failure_modes.condition: the per-employee wage change notices are not generated
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a bulk pay change produces a bulk notice obligation, which the workflow must produce

evidence_expected: Validation results per row with the rule that failed.
The simulation of the aggregate effect the approval bound to.
Per-row commit outcome and the excluded set.

title: Explain how a field's value came to be across a migration
preconditions: Tenant acme. A worker's job title effective 2024-03-01 is queried on 2026-09-08.
A data migration in 2025-01 overwrote pre-2024 revision history for that field.
The auditor has an AUDIT_EVIDENCE purpose.
story: As an auditor, I want a gap in the revision chain to be disclosed rather than smoothed over, so that I know the difference between a complete history and a truncated one
scenario: The revision chain is assembled with effective-at, known-at, actor and source authority per link. The chain is complete from 2025-01 forward. Before that a migration overwrote history, so the earliest retained revision is the migration itself, attributed to a system actor. The answer discloses the gap and its boundary rather than presenting the migration record as though it were the original assertion. A smooth-looking chain that hides a migration is a lie.

acceptance_criteria.given: the chain has a gap caused by a migration
acceptance_criteria.then: the gap and its boundary are disclosed rather than the migration record standing in for the original

acceptance_criteria.given: a revision's actor is a system
acceptance_criteria.then: it says so rather than attributing the change to the last human who touched anything

acceptance_criteria.given: the caller may read the current value but not the historical one
acceptance_criteria.then: the current value is returned and the history is DENIED, which is a legitimate and different answer

acceptance_criteria.given: the read completes
acceptance_criteria.then: zero writes and a zero-effect receipt

data_read.people: revision chains for the field
data_read.provenance: source authority and actor per revision
data_read.privacy: field classification

authorization_and_disclosure: The auditor receives PARTIAL disclosure: the chain and the disclosed gap are shown and any field outside their purpose is DENIED by name.
The subject is not notified of an audit read under a lawful purpose.

failure_modes.condition: the migration record is presented as the original assertion
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the chain looks complete and the auditor draws a wrong conclusion

failure_modes.condition: the gap is omitted
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the answer is materially misleading in exactly the way an audit exists to catch

evidence_expected: Revision chain with both time axes per link.
The disclosed gap and its boundary.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Compare local state against a stale external system
preconditions: Tenant acme. A cross-system diff runs against a benefits carrier at 2026-07-19T08:00.
The local watermark is current; the carrier's last file is dated 2026-07-12.
412 differences are found.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want a seven-day lag to be separated from real disagreement, so that we do not generate 400 false repairs
scenario: Both sides are read with their watermarks. The carrier's watermark is seven days behind. Of 412 differences, 389 involve records changed locally inside that seven-day window, so they are reported as possibly-timing with the lag stated. Twenty-three involve records unchanged for months, which cannot be explained by the lag and are real disagreements. Treating all 412 as drift would produce 389 unnecessary repairs and would train everyone to ignore the report.

acceptance_criteria.given: the carrier's watermark is seven days behind
acceptance_criteria.then: differences involving records changed inside the lag window are reported as possibly-timing with the lag stated

acceptance_criteria.given: 23 differences involve long-unchanged records
acceptance_criteria.then: they are reported as real disagreements and are the ones worth acting on

acceptance_criteria.given: a field exists on one side only
acceptance_criteria.then: reported as unmapped rather than as a difference; an unmapped field is a mapping gap

acceptance_criteria.given: the caller may not read a field on either side
acceptance_criteria.then: the field is DENIED in the diff rather than silently excluded, so the caller knows the comparison is partial

data_read.people: local authoritative state
data_read.integration: external state and its watermark
data_read.privacy: field classification for the diff output

authorization_and_disclosure: The administrator receives FULL disclosure of both watermarks and the classification; any field outside their authorization is DENIED in the diff.

failure_modes.condition: all differences are treated as drift
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 389 false repairs and a report nobody trusts

failure_modes.condition: the external watermark is unavailable
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the comparison is reported as unclassifiable rather than presented as drift

evidence_expected: Both watermarks, so a timing difference is distinguishable.
Per-field difference with its materiality and classification.
Field authorization applied to the output.

title: Promote configuration that would repin a running instance
preconditions: Tenant acme. Configuration package CFG-2026-31 changes an approval threshold rule.
Eleven workflow instances are running pinned to the current rule version.
The promotion authority is separate from the authoring authority.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want a promotion that would change a rule a running instance is pinned to be blocked, so that an in-flight approval is not re-scored halfway through
scenario: The package is diffed against the target environment. The simulation shows eleven running instances pinned to the rule version the package would supersede. Promoting would either repin them, changing the threshold mid flight, or leave them on a version the environment no longer exposes. The promotion is blocked. The choice is made explicitly: the eleven are allowed to complete on the old version, which is retained for that purpose, and the promotion activates for new instances only.

acceptance_criteria.given: eleven instances are pinned to the superseded version
acceptance_criteria.then: it is BLOCKED and the affected instances are named

acceptance_criteria.given: the decision is made explicitly
acceptance_criteria.then: the old version is retained for the running instances and the new version applies to new instances only

acceptance_criteria.given: the package was authored against a stale target
acceptance_criteria.then: the unexpected changes are shown and the promotion is REPLANNED; promoting a stale package silently reverts other work

acceptance_criteria.given: the activation partially applies
acceptance_criteria.then: a mixed version state is reported and the promotion is BLOCKED rather than reported successful

data_read.dataops: package contents, target configuration and prior promotions
data_read.workflow: in-flight instances and their pinned versions

data_written.dataops: the promotion record and its activation
data_written.compliance: the new active configuration version

authorization_and_disclosure: The promoter receives FULL disclosure of the diff and the affected instances; the instance owners are notified of their own instances only.

failure_modes.condition: the promotion repins running instances
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an approval threshold changes halfway through an approval, which nobody can explain afterwards

failure_modes.condition: a rollback is needed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: it is its own promotion of the prior version with its own approval; there is no unlogged undo

evidence_expected: The diff the approval bound to.
In-flight instance impact analysis.
Activation confirmation from the target.

title: Grant support access with the customer's approval
preconditions: Tenant acme. A support engineer needs read access to acme's payroll configuration to diagnose case SUP-3311.
Acme's policy requires customer approval for any support access.
The grant is scoped to configuration read only, for four hours.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the customer's own approval to gate access to their tenant, so that nobody inside the vendor can look at customer data on their own say-so
scenario: The engineer requests access citing SUP-3311 and the specific scope. The internal approver approves. Acme's policy requires customer approval, so the request is routed to acme's named administrator, who approves it in their own tenant. The grant is issued time-bound and scoped, attributable to the individual engineer rather than a shared support role. Every read is logged. After expiry acme receives an access report listing exactly what was read.

acceptance_criteria.given: acme's policy requires customer approval
acceptance_criteria.then: acme's own administrator approves in their tenant before any grant is issued

acceptance_criteria.given: the grant is issued
acceptance_criteria.then: it is time-bound, scoped to configuration read, and attributable to the individual rather than a shared role

acceptance_criteria.given: the engineer needs wider scope mid session
acceptance_criteria.then: a new request and approval is required; scope creep inside an active grant defeats the control

acceptance_criteria.given: the grant expires
acceptance_criteria.then: acme receives an access report listing exactly what was read

acceptance_criteria.given: the grant is used outside the cited case
acceptance_criteria.then: an incident opens; the log is what makes the misuse detectable

data_read.security: support policy, prior grants and scope definitions
data_read.tenant: acme's own approval policy

data_written.security: the grant record, the activity log and the access report

authorization_and_disclosure: Acme receives FULL disclosure of the access report; the engineer's individual actions are attributable rather than anonymous.

failure_modes.condition: a shared support role is used
failure_modes.expected_refusal: attribution is destroyed and the access report cannot say who read what

failure_modes.condition: the customer approver is unavailable during an outage
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the break-glass path applies with heavier approval and mandatory post-use review

evidence_expected: Customer approval where their policy requires it.
Per-action activity log attributable to the individual.
The access report delivered to the customer.

title: Rotate a credential while operations are in flight
preconditions: Tenant acme. A payroll provider credential expires 2026-06-30 with a 14-day rotation lead time.
The target supports overlapping credentials for 24 hours.
Forty operations are in flight at the cutover moment.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the old credential not to be retired while operations are still using it, so that a rotation does not become an outage
scenario: The expiry is detected against the lead time and a new credential is requested. It is verified against the target before anything is retired, because a rotation to an unverified credential is an outage waiting for the next operation. The target supports a 24-hour overlap, so both credentials are valid during the cutover. Forty in-flight operations drain on the old credential. Only when the drain completes is the old lease retired, and operations on the new credential are confirmed before the rotation closes.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new credential is issued
acceptance_criteria.then: verification against the target precedes any retirement of the old one

acceptance_criteria.given: forty operations are in flight
acceptance_criteria.then: the old credential is retired only once every in-flight operation has reached a terminal ExecutionState, so no operation is holding it when it is withdrawn

acceptance_criteria.given: the target does not support overlapping credentials
acceptance_criteria.then: a maintenance window is required and the plan says so rather than attempting a seamless cutover that will fail

acceptance_criteria.given: the rotation completes
acceptance_criteria.when: operations on the new credential are observed
acceptance_criteria.then: success on the new credential is confirmed before the rotation closes, rather than the retirement of the old lease being treated as completion

data_read.security: the lease, its expiry and the rotation policy
data_read.integration: in-flight operations using the credential

data_written.security: the new lease and the retired one's record

authorization_and_disclosure: Operations receives FULL disclosure of the rotation and its drain state; the credential values are DENIED to every reader.

failure_modes.condition: the new credential fails verification
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the rotation is BLOCKED and the old credential's expiry becomes an incident with a deadline

failure_modes.condition: the old credential is retired while operations are in flight
failure_modes.expected_refusal: those operations fail; the drain check exists to prevent it

evidence_expected: Verification of the new credential before cutover.
In-flight operation drain evidence.
The retirement record for the old lease.

title: Contain a suspected session takeover before confirming it
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-138580's session shows a login from an unusual location at 03:12 followed by a payment method change attempt.
The worker's registered mobile is on file.
The account can reach compensation and personal data for 40 workers.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want containment to happen before the investigation concludes, so that a real takeover is stopped in minutes rather than after an analysis
scenario: The signals are collected. Logs and session evidence are preserved first, because containment will destroy some of them. Sessions are then invalidated and re-authentication is required, before anyone decides whether the takeover is real. The worker is contacted out of band on their registered mobile and confirms they did not log in. The breach assessment runs on what the account could reach: compensation and personal data for 40 workers. Credentials are rotated and the account re-provisioned. The assessment is recorded whether or not notification is required.

acceptance_criteria.given: suspicious signals are detected
acceptance_criteria.then: logs and session evidence are preserved before containment, because containment destroys some of them

acceptance_criteria.given: containment is applied
acceptance_criteria.then: sessions are invalidated and re-authentication required before the investigation concludes

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker confirms it was not them
acceptance_criteria.then: the data classes within the account's reach determine which notification clocks start

acceptance_criteria.given: the signals turn out to be a false positive
acceptance_criteria.then: the containment stands and the worker re-authenticates; a false positive costs minutes

acceptance_criteria.given: no notification is required
acceptance_criteria.then: the assessment and its reasoning are recorded anyway, because the reasoning is what an auditor tests

data_read.security: sessions, devices and authentication history
data_read.identity: what the compromised identity could reach
data_read.privacy: the data classes within that reach

data_written.security: the incident record, containment actions and the breach assessment
data_written.identity: invalidated sessions and rotated credentials

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure through the out-of-band channel; the 40 workers whose data was reachable are notified only if the assessment requires it.

failure_modes.condition: containment is delayed pending confirmation
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the attacker keeps working while the analysis runs

failure_modes.condition: the out-of-band channel is the compromised one
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the contact warns nobody and the verification is worthless

evidence_expected: Preserved logs from before containment.
Out-of-band verification with the worker.
The breach assessment with its conclusion and reasoning.

title: Register a workload principal with no interactive path
preconditions: Tenant acme. A nightly reconciliation job needs a principal to read payroll and general ledger data.
A team requests an interactive account with a shared password so people can also log in as it.
The maximum authority the job needs is read-only across two domains.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want a workload principal to have no interactive credential, so that the job's identity is not a back door for people
scenario: The principal is created as a workload type bound to the job rather than to a person. The requested interactive password and shared use are refused twice over: a workload principal has no interactive path, and a shared credential destroys attribution regardless of principal type. The assurance level is derived from the maximum authority, which is read-only across payroll and general ledger. The job authenticates with a rotating workload credential.

acceptance_criteria.given: an interactive password is requested for a workload principal
acceptance_criteria.then: REJECT; a workload with an interactive path is a human account wearing a service label

acceptance_criteria.given: shared use is requested
acceptance_criteria.then: REJECT; a shared credential destroys attribution, which every other control depends on

acceptance_criteria.given: the maximum authority is read-only
acceptance_criteria.then: the required assurance follows the authority rather than being chosen by the requester

data_read.security: existing principals, the assurance policy and factor types
data_read.identity: the maximum authority the principal may hold

data_written.security: the principal record and its credential

authorization_and_disclosure: The job's owner receives FULL disclosure of the principal and its scope; the credential is DENIED to every reader after issue.

failure_modes.condition: the principal's authority later exceeds its assurance
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the grant is refused until the assurance is raised

failure_modes.condition: the team creates a personal account for the job instead
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the job's actions become attributable to a person who did not perform them

evidence_expected: The principal type and its binding.
The assurance derivation from the maximum authority.
The credential issue and its rotation policy.

title: Recover an account for a principal with sensitive authority
preconditions: Tenant acme. Payroll administrator W-138910 loses their hardware factor on 2026-05-22.
Their principal can release payroll runs.
Self-service recovery is available for ordinary principals.
story: As an employee, I want recovery for a sensitive principal to require a human verifier, so that the recovery path is not weaker than the thing it recovers
scenario: The worker starts recovery. Their principal can release payroll runs, which is above the sensitivity threshold for self-service recovery. The request routes to an assisted path where a verifier confirms identity through a channel independent of the lost factor. A temporary credential is issued with a two-hour expiry and forced enrollment of a new factor. The worker is notified through their personal email, which is not the channel being recovered. The temporary credential's expiry is verified after enrollment.

acceptance_criteria.given: the principal can release payroll runs
acceptance_criteria.then: self-service is refused and the assisted path with a human verifier is required

acceptance_criteria.given: identity is proofed
acceptance_criteria.then: the assurance of the proofing is at least as strong as the factor being replaced

acceptance_criteria.given: a temporary credential is issued
acceptance_criteria.then: it has a short expiry and forces enrollment of a new factor before ordinary access resumes

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker is notified
acceptance_criteria.then: it is independent of the one being recovered; a notification to the compromised channel warns nobody

acceptance_criteria.given: three recoveries occur on this principal in two months
acceptance_criteria.then: a security review opens; account recovery is a standard takeover route

data_read.security: the principal, its factors, prior recoveries and the assurance policy
data_read.people: the worker's independent contact points
data_read.identity: the authority the principal holds

data_written.security: the recovery record, the temporary credential and the new factor enrollment

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the recovery steps; the verifier's identity and the proofing method are recorded and FULL to security.

failure_modes.condition: self-service is used for a sensitive principal
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the recovery path becomes the account's real security level, which is then weaker than its authority

failure_modes.condition: the temporary credential does not expire
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a permanent credential issued under an exception, which is the worst outcome of a recovery

evidence_expected: Identity proofing method and its assurance.
Notification through an independent channel.
Temporary credential expiry and the new factor enrollment.

title: Run a scheduled report whose recipient lost their scope
preconditions: Tenant acme. Report RPT-220 runs monthly with three recipients.
One recipient moved to a different function on 2026-06-01 and lost scope over the reported population.
The report was defined in 2025 and its recipient list has not changed.
story: As an HR business partner, I want authorization to be evaluated per run rather than at definition time, so that a scheduled report does not keep delivering data to someone who lost access
scenario: The report runs on 2026-07-01. Authorization is evaluated for each recipient at run time, not from the definition. The moved recipient no longer has scope over the population. Their copy is produced with the out-of-scope rows suppressed and the suppression disclosed, so they can see the report is partial rather than assuming the population shrank. The change is recorded. Had authorization been evaluated once at definition, they would have received the full report for thirteen months.

acceptance_criteria.given: a recipient's authorization narrowed since the definition
acceptance_criteria.then: authorization is evaluated per recipient at run time and their copy is filtered accordingly

acceptance_criteria.given: rows are suppressed for one recipient
acceptance_criteria.then: the suppression is disclosed so they know the report is partial

acceptance_criteria.given: a recipient leaves the organization
acceptance_criteria.then: delivery stops, the schedule's BusinessState becomes SUSPENDED with the reason recorded, and a scheduled report to a departed employee is treated as a live exposure rather than a stale subscription

acceptance_criteria.given: the population is small enough to identify individuals
acceptance_criteria.then: the small-cell rule suppresses it and the suppression is stated

data_read.analytics: the report definition, dataset and watermark
data_read.privacy: field classification and suppression rules
data_read.people: recipient authorization

data_written.analytics: the report run, per-recipient outputs and delivery records

authorization_and_disclosure: Each recipient's disclosure is PARTIAL where their authorization has narrowed, with the suppressed rows DENIED rather than silently absent.

failure_modes.condition: authorization is evaluated once at definition
failure_modes.expected_refusal: stale access persists in reporting, which is the most common way old permissions keep delivering data

failure_modes.condition: the whole run fails because one recipient lacks scope
failure_modes.expected_refusal: REJECT that behaviour; the run produces per-recipient outputs

evidence_expected: Per-run authorization evaluation per recipient.
Suppression record showing what each recipient did not see.
Dataset watermark, so the copies are comparable.

title: Redefine a metric without restating its history
preconditions: Tenant acme. Voluntary turnover metric MET-14 v1 excluded fixed-term endings.
Version 2, effective 2026-07-01, includes them.
Eighteen monthly observations exist under v1.
story: As a finance partner, I want a definition change to create a new version rather than restate the trend, so that the trend line stays reconcilable
scenario: The metric is redefined to include fixed-term endings. A new version is published rather than the definition being edited. The eighteen existing observations keep v1 and are not restated. Observations from 2026-07-01 cite v2. A chart spanning the boundary shows the version change rather than a smooth line, which is uncomfortable and correct: a restated trend nobody can reconcile is how metrics lose credibility.

acceptance_criteria.given: the definition changes
acceptance_criteria.then: a new version is created and the eighteen prior observations keep v1

acceptance_criteria.given: a chart spans the version boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: the version change is shown rather than the series being silently restated

acceptance_criteria.given: an observation's stored inputs are no longer retrievable
acceptance_criteria.then: it stands but is marked unverifiable rather than being presented as reproducible

data_read.analytics: metric definitions and prior observations
data_read.people: the population the metric measures

data_written.analytics: the new metric version and its observations

authorization_and_disclosure: Every reader receives FULL disclosure of which metric version produced each observation; the definition itself is not restricted.

failure_modes.condition: history is restated under the new definition
failure_modes.expected_refusal: REJECT; a restated trend line that nobody can reconcile destroys the metric's value

failure_modes.condition: two teams define the same-named metric differently
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the naming collision is rejected at definition

evidence_expected: Formula version with each observation.
Stored inputs, so an observation can be recomputed.
The version boundary.

title: Build an evidence package that fails its own verification
preconditions: Tenant acme. An evidence package covers 1,840 ledger events for Q2 2026.
The manifest lists 1,840 parts. Verification finds 1,839 present and one digest mismatch.
The package is intended for an external auditor.
story: As an auditor, I want a package that fails verification not to be released, so that evidence that cannot verify itself is not evidence
scenario: The package is assembled with a manifest carrying a digest per part. Verification runs: every listed part present, no unlisted part, digests match, chain intact, head attested, no tenant leak. One part's digest does not match its manifest entry. The package is not released. Investigation shows the part was regenerated after the manifest was built, which is a build ordering defect rather than tampering, but the package is rebuilt rather than the manifest being patched to match.

acceptance_criteria.given: one part's digest does not match the manifest
acceptance_criteria.then: the package is not released and the mismatch is reported with the part named

acceptance_criteria.given: the cause is a build ordering defect
acceptance_criteria.then: the package is rebuilt rather than the manifest being patched to match the part

acceptance_criteria.given: an unlisted part is present
acceptance_criteria.then: it is reported; extra content is as much a defect as missing content

acceptance_criteria.given: the chain or the epoch coverage is incomplete
acceptance_criteria.then: the package is not released; a gap in the chain is what the verification exists to find

acceptance_criteria.given: verification passes
acceptance_criteria.then: the verification report is attached, which is what supports its authentication

data_read.documents: artifacts referenced by the events
data_read.privacy: classification limiting what may be included

data_written.operations: the evidence package, its manifest and its verification report

authorization_and_disclosure: The external auditor receives FULL disclosure of the package and its verification report; a tenant leak finding would block release entirely.

failure_modes.condition: the manifest is patched to match the part
failure_modes.expected_refusal: REJECT; the manifest is the assertion and patching it to fit destroys its meaning

failure_modes.condition: the package is released with a known mismatch and a note
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the note does not repair the evidence; it documents that it is not evidence

evidence_expected: Manifest with a digest per part.
Verification findings, including the mismatch.
Chain and epoch coverage proof.

title: Analyse turnover and refuse a per-person flight risk score
preconditions: Tenant acme. A unit's voluntary turnover is 19 percent against a 12 percent company figure.
The manager asks for per-person attrition risk scores for their eleven reports.
The model can produce them.
story: As a manager, I want an individual flight risk score not to be handed to a manager, so that an analysis does not quietly become a decision about a person
scenario: The unit-level analysis is produced with the declared turnover definition, the cohort and the period. The manager then asks for per-person scores. The model can compute them, and that is precisely the problem: an individual flight-risk score handed to a manager changes how that person is treated, which makes the analysis a decision. The request is denied. The unit-level drivers are provided instead, which is what actually supports a management response.

acceptance_criteria.given: per-person risk scores are requested
acceptance_criteria.then: DENIED; an individual score handed to a manager changes how that person is treated and the analysis becomes a decision

acceptance_criteria.given: the unit-level analysis is produced
acceptance_criteria.then: the turnover definition used is recorded, since voluntary and total turnover give different answers

acceptance_criteria.given: a cut identifies an individual by combination
acceptance_criteria.then: the cell is suppressed and the suppression is disclosed

acceptance_criteria.given: protected characteristics are requested as a cut
acceptance_criteria.then: DENY without a permitting purpose, and the refusal does not reveal the cohort size

data_read.people: population, terminations and tenure
data_read.talent: ratings and engagement signals where a purpose permits
data_read.compensation: pay position, subject to authorization

data_written.analytics: the analysis result with its model version and controls

authorization_and_disclosure: The manager receives PARTIAL disclosure: unit-level drivers are disclosed and per-person risk scores are DENIED uniformly.
Per-person scores are refused uniformly, so the refusal does not signal anything about any individual.

failure_modes.condition: the score is provided with a caveat that it is only indicative
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the caveat does not survive contact with a manager who has a number next to a name

failure_modes.condition: the analysis is presented as establishing causation
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the result carries an explicit statement of what it does not establish

evidence_expected: The turnover definition used.
Suppression record for small cells.
The refusal of the per-person request.

title: Render a dashboard tile the viewer may not see
preconditions: Tenant acme. Dashboard DSH-07 has six tiles; one shows compensation distribution.
A front-line manager may see headcount and absence tiles but not compensation.
The dashboard was designed for directors.
story: As a manager, I want a tile I may not see to be marked denied rather than hidden, so that I know the picture is partial

It renders as DENIED by name rather than being removed from the layout, so the manager knows the dashboard has six tiles and they can see five. A hidden tile would let them draw conclusions from an incomplete picture without knowing it was incomplete.

acceptance_criteria.then: the tile renders as DENIED by name rather than being hidden from the layout

acceptance_criteria.given: two viewers with different authorization open the same dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: their totals differ legitimately and the disclosure record explains it

acceptance_criteria.given: the viewer's authorization narrows between renders
acceptance_criteria.then: it reflects the narrowed authorization; authorization evaluated once at publication is how stale access persists

title: A caller replays an approved proposal digest against a new proposal

title: Move a candidate to a talent pool after rejection
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. Candidate C-7712 is rejected for REQ-9612 on 2026-02-11.

title: Provision a contractor with a narrower entitlement set
preconditions: Tenant acme. Contingent worker C-9012 starts 2026-05-11 on a six-month engagement.
The employee template for the same role grants 14 entitlements; the contingent template grants 6.
The engagement end date is known at provisioning.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the contingent template to apply rather than the employee one, so that a non-employee does not get an employee's access because the role matched
scenario: The role matches an employee role, and the template resolution takes worker type as well as role. The contingent template grants six entitlements rather than fourteen. Each grant carries the engagement end date as its expiry, so access ends with the engagement rather than depending on someone remembering. The narrower set is also what keeps the co-employment indicators from tripping.

acceptance_criteria.then: the contingent template applies and the employee template's eight extra entitlements are not granted

title: Deprovision a worker who moves to a contingent engagement
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-164880 resigns 2026-08-14 and returns as a contractor 2026-09-01.
Their employee access is revoked at separation; the contingent engagement grants a narrower set.
The identity is the same Person.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the employee access to be revoked even though the person returns, so that continuous access is not created by a gap nobody enforced
scenario: The worker separates and returns eighteen days later in a different capacity. The temptation is to leave access in place because the person is coming back. Employee access is revoked at separation and the contingent engagement provisions its own narrower set under the same Person.

acceptance_criteria.then: employee access is revoked in full rather than being left in place for convenience

data_read.people: the separation, the engagement and the shared Person

data_written.identity: the revocations and the new contingent grants

authorization_and_disclosure: The person receives FULL disclosure of what they can access in each capacity.

The absence of any entitlement spanning the gap.

title: Track an equipment shipment to a remote starter
preconditions: Tenant acme. A laptop ships to worker W-165210 on 2026-04-20 for a 2026-04-27 start.

title: Offboard a worker across three legal entities
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-165540 holds concurrent employments at Acme US Inc, Acme Research LLC and Acme Services Inc.

acceptance_criteria.given: one entity's final pay is late

title: A departing worker attempts to grant themselves access before leaving

title: A caller enumerates workers by probing a search filter
preconditions: Tenant acme. A recruiter holds a search scope covering their own requisitions' candidate pool only.
They issue 340 searches in ten minutes with single-character surname prefixes.
Two searches return results; 338 return empty.
story: As a recruiter, I want an enumeration pattern to be detected even though each search is individually permitted, so that a permitted capability used at scale is not automatically fine
scenario: Each individual search is within the recruiter's scope and each individual refusal or empty result discloses nothing. The pattern is the problem: 340 single-character prefix searches in ten minutes is enumeration rather than recruitment. The rate and shape trigger a detection that suspends the search scope pending review. The suspension is not a finding of misconduct; it is a containment, and the review may well conclude it was a badly written script.

acceptance_criteria.given: each search is individually within scope
acceptance_criteria.then: each returns only disclosable subjects and each refusal is identical

acceptance_criteria.then: the search scope is suspended pending review, which is a containment rather than a finding

acceptance_criteria.then: it states the suspension and the review route rather than accusing them

acceptance_criteria.given: the review concludes it was a script
acceptance_criteria.then: the restoration is recorded and the detection threshold is reviewed rather than simply raised

acceptance_criteria.given: the enumeration had succeeded in mapping the population
acceptance_criteria.then: what was disclosable to that scope is what was learned, which bounds the exposure and is worth computing

data_read.security: the search scope, the rate history and the detection thresholds

data_written.security: the enumeration detection event and the scope suspension

failure_modes.expected_refusal: enumeration is exactly the case where per-request authorization is insufficient

failure_modes.condition: the scope is revoked permanently on the first detection
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a badly written script becomes a career event; suspension pending review is the proportionate response

evidence_expected: The per-search scope evaluations.
The enumeration detection with its rate and shape.
The suspension, the review and the restoration.

title: Certify an entitlement whose owner has left

title: Review my own access and report something I do not recognize

title: Record a performance rating and release it to the worker
preconditions: Tenant acme. Manager Ines Duarte submits a rating for W-167190 on 2026-11-20.
Calibration is complete and the second-level approval is recorded.

scenario: The rating is calibrated and approved. It is held until the cycle's release date of 2026-12-01 rather than becoming visible to the worker on approval. Erasing the record would destroy the evidence the investigation rests on and would also remove the reporter's account, which is not the requester's data alone. The refusal rests on Article 17(3): the processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims and for compliance with a legal obligation. The ground is stated, the requester is told which categories are refused and why, and their right to complain to the supervisory authority is included.

acceptance_criteria.given: the record contains a third party's account

acceptance_criteria.given: the refusal is issued

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester's contact and preference data is also in scope

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives PARTIAL disclosure: erased categories are confirmed and refused categories are DENIED with their ground named.

The requester named the investigation in their own request, so its contents are DENIED to them by name while it is live rather than concealed; the reporter's identity is WITHHELD, and the response does not confirm that a reporter's account is among the refused categories.

failure_modes.condition: the request is ignored
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the one-month deadline is missed and the failure to respond is its own violation

failure_modes.condition: the investigation record is erased
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the evidence is destroyed, the reporter's account is lost, and the erasure is itself unlawful under Article 17(3)

failure_modes.condition: the refusal is issued with no ground
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester cannot challenge it, which defeats the right to complain

evidence_expected: The request with its receipt date and the one-month clock.
The per-category decision with its Article 17(3) ground.
The response and its delivery to an authenticated recipient.

title: Restrict processing rather than erase it
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Netherlands BV. A worker contests the accuracy of a performance rating on 2026-09-15.
They request restriction of processing while the accuracy is verified.
The rating feeds a merit cycle running now.
story: As a compliance officer, I want restriction to stop the processing without deleting the record, so that the disputed record is preserved while it is not used
scenario: The worker contests accuracy and requests restriction rather than erasure. Restriction means the record is retained but not processed beyond storage while the accuracy is verified. The exclusion from the cycle inputs.
The verification outcome and any rectification with its Article 19 notifications.

title: Assess a breach that reached a processor's sub-processor
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. A payroll processor's sub-processor suffers a breach on 2026-11-03 affecting 1,204 German workers.
The processor notifies acme on 2026-11-05.
GDPR requires controller notification to the authority within 72 hours of awareness.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the controller's awareness clock to start when the processor notified rather than when the breach occurred, so that we neither over-report a breach we did not know about nor under-report one we did
scenario: The breach occurred on 2026-11-03 at a sub-processor. Acme is the controller and became aware on 2026-11-05 when the processor notified it. The 72-hour clock runs from acme's awareness, not from the breach, and not from the sub-processor's own awareness. That distinction is recorded explicitly because both errors are common: starting from the breach over-reports lateness, and starting from a later internal triage under-reports it. The processor's own delay in notifying is a separate finding against the processor.

acceptance_criteria.given: the breach occurred before acme was notified
acceptance_criteria.then: it runs from acme's awareness on 2026-11-05 rather than from the breach date

acceptance_criteria.given: the processor delayed notifying
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a separate finding against the processor under the Article 28 contract rather than part of acme's own timeline

acceptance_criteria.given: the affected workers are in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: the lead supervisory authority and any concerned authorities are identified rather than assumed

acceptance_criteria.given: the risk to individuals is high
acceptance_criteria.then: individual notification is required and is separate from the authority notification

acceptance_criteria.given: the 72 hours would be missed
acceptance_criteria.then: it is made without undue further delay with the reasons for the delay stated, which the regulation permits

data_read.privacy: the processing activities, the processor contract and the affected categories
data_read.people: the 1,204 affected workers
data_read.integration: the processor and its sub-processor chain

data_written.privacy: the breach assessment, the authority notification and any individual notifications

authorization_and_disclosure: The affected workers receive FULL disclosure where the Article 34 assessment requires it.
The processor's internal incident detail is DENIED to acme beyond what the contract requires it to share.

failure_modes.condition: the clock is started from the breach date
failure_modes.expected_refusal: lateness is overstated and the report says something untrue about acme's conduct

failure_modes.condition: the clock is started from internal triage
failure_modes.expected_refusal: lateness is understated, which is the more serious error

failure_modes.condition: the sub-processor was not in the assessed chain
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the transfer and vendor assessments were incomplete, which is its own finding

evidence_expected: The awareness timestamp and its basis in the processor's notification.
The processor's delay, recorded as a separate finding.
The authority notification and any individual notifications with their assessments.

title: Consult workers before deploying a monitoring change
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Netherlands BV. A change adds device location logging to company laptops on 2026-07-01.
The works council has codetermination rights over monitoring measures.
The change is technically ready.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the works council agreement to be a precondition rather than a notification, so that the deployment does not happen before the agreement exists
scenario: The change is ready to deploy. In the Netherlands a works council has codetermination rights over monitoring measures, which means agreement rather than notification: deploying first and informing afterwards is not a lesser version of the process, it is a different and unlawful one. The deployment is blocked until agreement is recorded. The council asks for the retention period to be shortened and agreement follows.

acceptance_criteria.given: the works council has codetermination rights
acceptance_criteria.then: it is BLOCKED until agreement is recorded, because agreement is a precondition rather than a notification

acceptance_criteria.given: the council requests a change
acceptance_criteria.then: the revised proposal is what agreement attaches to, and the original is superseded

acceptance_criteria.given: agreement is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the agreement, its scope and its date are retained with the monitoring declaration

data_read.privacy: the monitoring purposes, categories and retention
data_read.labor: the works council's codetermination rights
data_read.people: the workers in scope

data_written.privacy: the monitoring declaration and the agreement record

authorization_and_disclosure: Workers receive FULL disclosure of the monitoring notice after agreement.
The council's internal deliberation is DENIED to the employer beyond its formal position.

failure_modes.condition: the change is deployed and the council is informed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: codetermination is not notification and the deployment is unlawful

failure_modes.condition: agreement is recorded for an earlier version of the proposal
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the agreement does not cover what was deployed

evidence_expected: The codetermination determination and its basis.
The agreement, its scope and its date.
The revised proposal it attaches to.

title: Produce a document with a native format the requester can use
preconditions: Tenant acme. A production request covers 1,140 documents on 2026-08-19.
The requester specifies a native format with metadata preserved.
Redaction is required on 212 of them.
story: As a compliance officer, I want redaction not to be the reason the whole production drops to images, so that the requester gets a usable production rather than a stack of pictures
scenario: Redaction on 212 documents does not require the other 928 to be flattened to images. Producing everything as images because some needed redaction is a common and expensive shortcut that destroys the metadata the requester specified. The 928 are produced natively with metadata; the 212 are redacted and produced in a format that carries what survives the redaction, with the redaction log accompanying them.

acceptance_criteria.given: 212 of 1,140 require redaction
acceptance_criteria.then: the other 928 are produced natively with metadata rather than the whole set being flattened

acceptance_criteria.given: the 212 are redacted
acceptance_criteria.then: the redacted content is removed from the bytes and the redaction log accompanies them

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester specified a native format
acceptance_criteria.then: the format is honoured where redaction does not prevent it, and the exceptions are named

acceptance_criteria.then: the metadata is checked as well as the body, because that is where redactions commonly leak

acceptance_criteria.then: the per-redaction basis answers it without disclosing the redacted content

data_read.documents: the source artifacts, their formats and their metadata
data_read.privacy: the redaction bases and the third-party data classes

data_written.documents: the production set, the redacted copies and the redaction log

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives FULL disclosure of the 928 and PARTIAL disclosure of the 212, with the redacted content DENIED and its basis stated per redaction.
The unredacted originals are WITHHELD from the requester and retained under their own controls.

title: Countersign a document after the worker signs
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-169170 signs a relocation repayment agreement on 2026-05-11.
The employer countersignature is required for execution.
The countersignature is applied on 2026-05-14.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the document to be unexecuted until both signatures exist, so that nobody relies on a half-signed agreement
scenario: The worker signs on 2026-05-11. The document is not executed: it has one of two required signatures. Treating it as executed at that point would let the relocation payment proceed against an agreement the employer had not countersigned, which is exactly the gap a worker would later point at. The countersignature on 2026-05-14 executes it, and both signatures bind the same document digest.

acceptance_criteria.then: the document is not executed and dependent actions are blocked

acceptance_criteria.given: the second signature is applied
acceptance_criteria.then: both signatures bind the same digest and the execution date is the later one

acceptance_criteria.then: the first signature's digest no longer matches and a fresh ceremony is required for both parties

data_read.documents: the document, its digest and its signature requirements
data_read.people: both signers and their authentication

data_written.documents: both signatures and the execution state

authorization_and_disclosure: Both parties receive FULL disclosure of the execution state and both signatures.

The ceremony evidence for both.

title: Look up a document template's current version
preconditions: Tenant acme. Template TPL-0440 for an offer letter has three published versions.

title: Retain a document past its schedule for a business reason
preconditions: Tenant acme. A design document reaches its seven-year retention on 2026-10-01.
The engineering team asks to retain it because a product still depends on it.

story: As a compliance officer, I want a business retention need to change the schedule rather than being an exception to it, so that the schedule stays true rather than being routinely overridden
scenario: The team asks to keep a document past its schedule. Granting a one-off exception would leave the schedule saying seven years while the practice says otherwise, and the next request would follow the same path. The document's class is reviewed instead: if a product depends on design documents beyond seven years, the class's retention is wrong and is changed with its own approval. The document is retained under the corrected schedule rather than as an exception.

acceptance_criteria.then: the class's retention is reviewed rather than a one-off exception being granted

acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded as an exception with an expiry and an owner, so it does not become the invisible norm

data_read.privacy: the retention schedule and its approval history

data_written.privacy: the class retention change or the recorded exception

The resulting disposition decision.

title: Verify an evidence package a customer will rely on
preconditions: Tenant acme. A customer requests an evidence package covering 90 days of approval decisions.

title: Look up a connector's current health state
preconditions: Tenant acme. Connector CN-0440 to a benefits carrier is healthy on 2026-03-02.

title: Retry a connector operation that failed transiently
preconditions: Tenant acme. A carrier enrollment operation fails with a gateway timeout on 2026-04-11T02:14.

acceptance_criteria.then: it uses the same idempotency key rather than a new one

acceptance_criteria.given: three attempts are exhausted
acceptance_criteria.then: it moves to UNKNOWN with an investigation rather than a fourth blind attempt

data_written.integration: the retry attempts and the eventual outcome

authorization_and_disclosure: Operations receives FULL disclosure of every attempt and its result.

title: Migrate a connector to a new authentication method

title: Configure a connector's rate limit to match the partner's
preconditions: Tenant acme. A learning provider publishes a limit of 60 requests per minute.

The sync outcomes before and after.

title: Detect that a partner silently changed a field's meaning

scenario: The 500 synthetic workers are generated with identifiers in a reserved prefix that production never issues. title: Attribute a conformance failure to the fixture rather than the system
preconditions: Tenant acme. A conformance scenario asserting a segregation-of-duties block fails on 2026-06-18.
The fixture's approver principal lost the role it needed when a role template changed.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a real defect is dismissed and the attribution stops being evidence of anything

The recorded attribution with the system's behaviour.

title: Assess a control whose evidence is a sample rather than a population
preconditions: Tenant acme. A control over termination access revocation is assessed on 2026-09-14.
The population is 412 terminations in the period; the sample is 25.
All 25 pass.
story: As an auditor, I want the sample method and size to be part of the conclusion rather than a footnote, so that the strength of the conclusion is visible with it
scenario: Twenty-five of 412 terminations are sampled and all pass. The conclusion is that the control operated effectively on the sample, with the sampling method and the size stated in the conclusion itself. Stating only that the control passed would imply the population was tested. The distinction matters because a 6 percent sample supports a materially weaker claim than a full population test.

acceptance_criteria.given: a sample rather than a population is tested
acceptance_criteria.then: the method and size are part of the conclusion rather than a footnote

acceptance_criteria.given: all 25 sampled items pass

acceptance_criteria.given: the sample is drawn
acceptance_criteria.then: it is reproducible, so a reviewer can draw the same sample and check it

data_read.compliance: the control, its assessment and the sampling method
data_read.people: the 412 terminations forming the population

data_written.compliance: the assessment with its sample and conclusion

authorization_and_disclosure: The auditor receives FULL disclosure of the sampled items and the method.
The 387 unsampled terminations are DENIED to the assessment beyond the population count.

failure_modes.condition: the conclusion omits the sample size
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a 6 percent test reads as a population test

failure_modes.condition: the sampling method is not reproducible
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the sample cannot be checked and the conclusion rests on trust

evidence_expected: The population count and the sample.
The reproducible sampling method.
The conclusion scoped to the sample.

title: Retire a control whose regulation no longer applies

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a retention schedule is overridden by an unrelated retirement

evidence_expected: The repeal and its effective date.
The remaining bases check.
The retired control with its interval and its resolvable assessments.

title: Measure a program against a baseline captured before it started
preconditions: Tenant acme. A manager coaching program runs 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30.

story: As an HR business partner, I want the measurement to be on the cohort that was measured at baseline rather than on whoever is present at the end, so that the number is not improved by attrition

title: See what a provisioning request is waiting on

title: Submit a cross-domain change that one domain refuses

The absence of any commit.

title: Compute contingent tenure across a break in engagement
preconditions: Tenant acme. Contractor C-3305 was engaged 2024-09-02 to 2025-11-28, then re-engaged 2026-02-16.

title: Diagnose drift between a projection and the ledger and bound the repair
preconditions: Tenant acme. A benefits eligibility projection disagrees with the ledger for 214 workers on 2026-07-06.

Rebuilding the whole projection would fix it and would also destroy the evidence of what drifted and why. The repair is bounded to the 214: their divergences are captured first, the cause is traced to a handler that dropped a specific event type between 2026-06-18 and 2026-06-24, and only those 214 are replayed. The rebuild remains available if the bounded repair fails.

acceptance_criteria.then: it covers the events in that range for those workers rather than all events for all workers

acceptance_criteria.given: the bounded repair fails to converge
acceptance_criteria.then: the rebuild is then a decision with its own approval rather than the first move

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the only record of what was wrong is destroyed by the fix

evidence_expected: The drifted set with its divergences captured pre-repair.
The traced cause with its date range and handler.
The bounded repair plan and its scope.

title: Prove that a repair converged rather than assuming it

title: A support principal reads an audit trail to find a suppressed entry
preconditions: Tenant acme. A support engineer with a valid grant reads a worker's audit trail on 2026-10-27.

title: Resolve a span-of-control violation created by a resignation

title: A departing worker exports a report they will not be able to read tomorrow

title: Recover a workflow instance whose external call outcome is unknown

Without one the principal is suspended rather than left running, and suspension is reversible in a way that a year of unowned access is not.
