acceptance_criteria.then: every principal they sponsor is surfaced and requires a new sponsor before the last day

acceptance_criteria.given: no new sponsor is named by the last day
acceptance_criteria.then: the principal is suspended rather than continuing unowned

acceptance_criteria.given: a new sponsor accepts
acceptance_criteria.then: it is an acceptance by the new sponsor with its own RequestState rather than an assignment made on their behalf

data_read.security: the principal, its sponsor and its entitlements
data_read.people: the sponsor's employment end date

data_written.security: the re-sponsorship or the suspension

authorization_and_disclosure: The new sponsor receives FULL disclosure of the principal's entitlements before accepting.
The principal's credential value is DENIED to the sponsor, who owns the accountability rather than the secret.

failure_modes.condition: the principal keeps running unowned
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an entitlement set nobody answers for persists until an access review finds it

failure_modes.condition: a new sponsor is assigned without accepting
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the accountability is nominal and the next review finds the same gap

evidence_expected: The sponsorship record and its history.
The offboarding surfacing of sponsored principals.
The acceptance or the suspension.

title: Approve a timecard that contains an unresolved exception
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-170420's timecard for the period ending 2026-05-15 has one unresolved missing punch.
The manager approves the timecard on 2026-05-17.
The payroll cutoff is 2026-05-18.
story: As a manager, I want the approval to be refused while an exception is unresolved rather than approving around it, so that an approved timecard means the hours were reviewed
scenario: The timecard carries an unresolved missing punch. Approving it would produce an approved timecard containing hours nobody determined, and the approval is the artifact a later wage claim is tested against. The approval is refused with the exception named. The manager resolves the punch, which is a separate recorded act, and then approves. Two acts rather than one, because they are two decisions.

acceptance_criteria.given: an exception is unresolved
acceptance_criteria.then: the approval is refused, the timecard's BusinessState stays UNAPPROVED, and the exception and its date are named

acceptance_criteria.given: the exception is resolved
acceptance_criteria.then: it succeeds, and the resolution and the approval are two separate recorded acts

acceptance_criteria.given: the cutoff arrives with the exception unresolved
acceptance_criteria.then: the timecard is excluded from the run with the reason recorded, rather than being included unapproved

data_read.time: the timecard, its punches and the exception
data_read.payroll: the run cutoff

data_written.time: the exception resolution and the approval

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the exception, its resolution and the approval.
The manager's queue of other workers' exceptions is DENIED to the worker.

failure_modes.condition: the approval covers an unresolved exception
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an approved timecard contains hours nobody determined

failure_modes.condition: the timecard is included in the run unapproved
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the run pays hours that were never reviewed, which is the harder error to unwind

evidence_expected: The exception and its resolution.
The approval, separate from the resolution.
The exclusion if the cutoff passes unresolved.

title: See which project my hours were charged to
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-170430 logged 38 hours in the period ending 2026-06-12.
The hours split across three projects: 20, 12 and 6.
One project is billable to an external client.
story: As an employee, I want the allocation to be visible to me by project, so that I can tell whether my time landed where I put it
scenario: The view shows 38 hours split 20, 12 and 6 across three named projects with the totals reconciling. The billable project is not distinguished, because billability is a commercial fact rather than one about the worker's time, and showing it invites a worker to allocate by billability rather than by what they did.

acceptance_criteria.given: hours split across three projects
acceptance_criteria.then: each project and its hours are shown and the parts sum to the recorded total

acceptance_criteria.given: one project is billable
acceptance_criteria.then: billability is not shown, because it is a commercial attribute rather than a fact about the hours

acceptance_criteria.given: the allocation was changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.then: the change and its actor are visible to the worker

data_read.time: the logged hours and their project allocation
data_read.finance: the project definitions, without their billing attributes

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of their own allocation and any change to it.
Project billability and client rates are DENIED to the worker in this view by name.

failure_modes.condition: billability is shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: workers allocate by billability rather than by what they did, which corrupts the data at source

failure_modes.condition: a post-submission change is invisible
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker's record of their own time disagrees with the system and neither knows

evidence_expected: The allocation by project.
Any post-submission change with its actor.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Publish a schedule that breaches a predictive scheduling rule
preconditions: Tenant acme. A retail schedule for the week of 2026-07-06 is published on 2026-07-01 in Oregon.
Oregon requires 14 days advance notice of the written schedule.
Two workers are affected by a shift added five days out.
story: As a manager, I want the late change to compute its premium rather than being published as an ordinary change, so that the workers are paid what the rule requires without anyone remembering to
scenario: The schedule is published five days out against a 14-day requirement. The publication is not blocked, because a business sometimes has to change a schedule and the statute prices that rather than forbidding it. The premium is computed per affected worker and per changed shift, attached to the change, and flows to payroll. A worker who declines a shift added with less than the required rest or notice is recorded as declining without consequence.

acceptance_criteria.given: a schedule change falls inside the notice period
acceptance_criteria.then: the premium is computed per affected worker and per changed shift and attached to the change

acceptance_criteria.given: the premium is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: it flows as a distinct earning code rather than being folded into base hours

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker declines a shift added inside the notice period
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded as a permitted decline with no consequence attached, and the premium's ObligationState is unaffected by the decline

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker accepts the shift
acceptance_criteria.then: the premium is still owed, because acceptance does not waive it

data_read.time: the schedule, its publication history and the changed shifts
data_read.regulatory: the state predictive scheduling rule and its premium
data_read.people: the affected workers and their locations

data_written.time: the published change and the recorded declines
data_written.payroll: the premium earnings

authorization_and_disclosure: The affected workers receive FULL disclosure of the premium owed and the basis for it.
Other workers' schedules and premiums are DENIED to them beyond the shifts they are assigned to.

failure_modes.condition: the change is published as ordinary
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the premium is never computed and surfaces as a claim

failure_modes.condition: acceptance is treated as a waiver
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the premium is not paid on the shifts most likely to be accepted

evidence_expected: The publication times against the notice requirement.
The per-worker premium computation.
The declines recorded as permitted.

title: Set a goal that depends on someone else's goal
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-170440 sets a 2026 goal on 2026-02-10 that depends on a platform migration owned by another team.
The dependency is recorded as a link to that team's goal.
The other goal slips to 2027 in June.
story: As an employee, I want the dependency to be recorded so a slip elsewhere is visible on my goal, so that my rating does not absorb someone else's timeline
scenario: The goal depends on a migration owned by another team, and the dependency is a link rather than a note. When the depended-on goal slips to 2027, the dependent goal is flagged automatically. At review time the slip is visible as a fact rather than as the worker's explanation, which is the difference between a record and an argument.

acceptance_criteria.given: a goal depends on another goal
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a link to the other goal rather than free text

acceptance_criteria.given: the depended-on goal slips
acceptance_criteria.then: it is flagged with the slip and its date rather than the worker having to raise it

acceptance_criteria.given: the review runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the dependency and its slip are part of the record the assessment reads

data_read.talent: both goals, their dates and the dependency link

data_written.talent: the dependency link and the slip flag

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the depended-on goal's dates and its slip.
The other team's internal reasons for the slip are DENIED to them; the dates and the fact of the slip are disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: the dependency is free text
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a slip elsewhere is invisible until the worker argues it at review

failure_modes.condition: the dependent goal is auto-adjusted on the slip
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the adjustment is a decision the worker and their manager make rather than one the system makes for them

evidence_expected: Both goals and the dependency link.
The slip and the flag it produced.
The dependency as part of the review record.

title: Nominate a successor who does not know they are nominated
preconditions: Tenant acme. Three successors are identified for a critical role on 2026-09-08.
Two are internal and unaware; one asked to be considered.
The plan is reviewed annually by the executive committee.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the plan to be readable by its reviewers without becoming readable by its subjects, so that a succession plan is a planning artifact rather than a promise
scenario: Two of the three do not know they are on the plan. Disclosing it would convert a planning judgement into an expectation the business has not made, and removing someone later would then be a demotion rather than a plan revision. The plan is readable by the executive committee and the HR partner. Where a subject exercises a data subject right, the plan entry about them is disclosable and the comparative ranking against the other two is not, because that is as much about them as about the requester.

acceptance_criteria.given: a subject is on the plan and unaware
acceptance_criteria.when: the plan is read by an unauthorized reader
acceptance_criteria.then: it is WITHHELD, and no queue, notification or view signals that a plan entry exists

acceptance_criteria.given: the executive committee reviews the plan
acceptance_criteria.then: all three entries are disclosed with their assessments

acceptance_criteria.given: a subject exercises a data subject access right
acceptance_criteria.then: their own entry is disclosed and the comparative ranking against the other two is DENIED, because it is equally about them

acceptance_criteria.given: a subject is removed from the plan
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a plan revision with its own basis, and it is not communicated to the subject who was never told they were on it

data_read.talent: the plan, its entries and their assessments
data_read.people: the three subjects and the critical role

data_written.talent: the plan revision and the disclosure decisions

authorization_and_disclosure: The executive committee and the HR partner receive FULL disclosure of the plan.
The plan is WITHHELD from the two unaware subjects, including its existence; on a subject access request their own entry becomes FULL and the comparative ranking is DENIED.

failure_modes.condition: the plan is disclosed to its subjects
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a planning judgement becomes a promise and a later removal becomes a demotion

failure_modes.condition: a subject access request returns the comparative ranking
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester learns another person's assessment through their own right

evidence_expected: The plan entries and their assessments.
The disclosure decisions per reader class.
The plan revision on any removal.

title: Collect multi-rater feedback where one rater is the subject's report
preconditions: Tenant acme. A 360 collection for manager W-170450 runs 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-24.
Seven raters respond: three peers, three direct reports and one skip-level manager.
The reporting threshold for a rater group is three.
story: As a manager, I want the direct report group to be reported only in aggregate, so that a report can answer honestly about their own manager
scenario: Three direct reports respond, which meets the group threshold of three. Their responses are reported as a group without attribution, because a report identifying their own manager's weaknesses by name is not a system anyone answers honestly in. The skip-level manager is a group of one and is therefore not reported at all, which is the same rule applied consistently rather than an exception made for a senior rater.

acceptance_criteria.given: three direct reports respond
acceptance_criteria.then: their responses are aggregated without attribution and the group is named

acceptance_criteria.given: the skip-level manager is a group of one
acceptance_criteria.then: that group is not reported, and the rule applies to a senior rater exactly as to a junior one

acceptance_criteria.given: the subject asks who said what
acceptance_criteria.then: it is DENIED by name for the aggregated groups: the subject is told attribution exists and is not disclosed

data_read.talent: the collection, its raters and their group memberships
data_read.people: the reporting structure defining the groups

data_written.talent: the aggregated report and the suppressed group

authorization_and_disclosure: The subject receives PARTIAL disclosure: aggregated group results are FULL and per-rater attribution is DENIED.
The single-rater group's responses are WITHHELD entirely, so the report does not indicate that a skip-level rater responded.

failure_modes.condition: the skip-level response is included because the rater is senior
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a group of one is attributable and the rule stops meaning anything

failure_modes.condition: attribution is available to the subject's manager but not the subject
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the raters answered on a confidentiality promise that names no exceptions

evidence_expected: The rater groups and their sizes.
The aggregation and the suppressed group.
The confidentiality terms shown to raters at collection.

title: Screen an application against criteria fixed before the posting opened
preconditions: Tenant acme. Requisition R-5510 posted 2026-03-02 with published screening criteria.
An application arrives 2026-03-18 from a strong candidate who misses one stated criterion.
The hiring manager asks to relax that criterion for this candidate.
story: As a recruiter, I want a criterion change to apply to the whole pool rather than to one candidate, so that the criteria mean the same thing for everyone who applied
scenario: Relaxing a criterion for one candidate makes the published criteria a description of who was screened rather than a rule. The change is permitted and applies to the requisition: the criterion is revised, the revision is dated, and every application already screened against the old criterion is re-screened. Candidates rejected on that criterion are reconsidered rather than left rejected under a rule that no longer exists.

acceptance_criteria.given: a criterion is relaxed mid posting
acceptance_criteria.then: it applies to the requisition and is dated rather than being applied to one candidate

acceptance_criteria.given: applications were already screened on the old criterion
acceptance_criteria.then: they are re-screened and rejections on that criterion are reconsidered

acceptance_criteria.given: the change is requested for one candidate only
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, and the refusal names the pool that would be treated inconsistently

data_read.recruiting: the requisition, its criteria and the applications screened
data_read.compliance: the record retention requirements for applicant data

data_written.recruiting: the criterion revision and the re-screening outcomes

authorization_and_disclosure: Candidates receive FULL disclosure of the published criteria and of any reconsideration of their application.
The internal deliberation about the specific candidate is WITHHELD from every candidate, including the one it concerns.

failure_modes.condition: the criterion is relaxed for one candidate
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the published criteria describe who was screened rather than governing it, which is the shape of a disparate treatment claim

failure_modes.condition: the re-screening is skipped
failure_modes.expected_refusal: earlier applicants are rejected under a rule the later ones did not face

evidence_expected: The criteria with their versions and dates.
The screening outcomes under each version.
The reconsiderations produced by the revision.

title: See the interview panel assigned to a candidate
preconditions: Tenant acme. Candidate C-6620 has four interviews scheduled between 2026-05-11 and 2026-05-14.
Each interviewer has a named focus area.
One interviewer has not completed the required interviewer training.
story: As a hiring manager, I want the untrained interviewer to be visible before the interviews happen, so that the panel is fixed while it can still be fixed
scenario: The panel view shows four interviewers with their focus areas and their training states. The untrained interviewer is visible now, three days before the first interview, rather than in a later audit of who conducted structured interviews. Showing the training state on the panel is what makes it actionable rather than reportable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a panel is assigned
acceptance_criteria.then: each interviewer's focus area and interviewer training state are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: one interviewer is untrained
acceptance_criteria.then: the gap is visible before the first interview rather than in a later audit

acceptance_criteria.given: the panel covers all required focus areas
acceptance_criteria.then: the coverage is shown, so a missing area is as visible as a missing person

data_read.recruiting: the panel, the schedule and the focus areas
data_read.learning: the interviewers' training completions

authorization_and_disclosure: The hiring manager receives FULL disclosure of the panel and its training states.
The interviewers' other training records are DENIED to the hiring manager; only the interviewer training is disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: the training state is not shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the gap is found in an audit after the interviews, when nothing can be done

failure_modes.condition: all training records are shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an interview panel view becomes a route into colleagues' learning history

evidence_expected: The panel with focus areas and training states.
The focus area coverage.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Run an access review where the reviewer is the entitlement's own user
preconditions: Tenant acme. An access review campaign opens 2026-10-05 covering 1,140 entitlements.
For 26 of them the configured reviewer is the entitlement holder.
The campaign closes 2026-11-05.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the 26 self-reviews to be reassigned rather than certified by their own holders, so that a review means somebody else looked
scenario: Twenty-six entitlements are configured so that their holder is their reviewer, which produces twenty-six certifications that certify nothing. They are reassigned to the entitlement owner or, where none exists, to the holder's manager. The reassignment is recorded as a campaign event so the review's completeness figure counts them as reviewed by someone else rather than simply as reviewed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured reviewer is the entitlement holder
acceptance_criteria.then: the item is reassigned rather than being issued to the holder

acceptance_criteria.given: no entitlement owner exists
acceptance_criteria.then: it goes to the holder's manager and the missing owner is raised as a configuration finding

acceptance_criteria.given: the campaign completeness is reported
acceptance_criteria.then: reassigned items are counted as reviewed by another party rather than merged into an undifferentiated total

acceptance_criteria.given: the holder is also their own manager's manager in a small unit
acceptance_criteria.then: it escalates further up rather than resolving to a person in the holder's own chain of subordinates

data_read.identity: the entitlements, their reviewers and their owners
data_read.people: the reporting structure used for reassignment

data_written.identity: the reassignments and the campaign completeness figure

authorization_and_disclosure: Reviewers receive FULL disclosure of the entitlements assigned to them and their holders.
Entitlements outside a reviewer's assignment are WITHHELD, so the campaign does not disclose the wider entitlement landscape.

failure_modes.condition: the holder certifies their own entitlement
failure_modes.expected_refusal: twenty-six certifications assert nothing and the campaign's completeness figure is inflated

failure_modes.condition: the reassignment is invisible in the completeness figure
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a campaign with many self-reviews looks the same as one with none

evidence_expected: The self-review detection and its 26 items.
The reassignments and their targets.
The completeness figure distinguishing reassigned items.

title: Revoke access immediately where the revocation itself is the notice
preconditions: Tenant acme. An immediate involuntary termination is decided at 2026-08-27T09:40 for worker W-170460.
The worker is in the building and holds access to a customer data system.
The termination meeting is at 10:15.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the revocation to be sequenced against the meeting rather than run at an arbitrary moment, so that the worker does not learn they are terminated from a locked screen
scenario: Revoking at 09:40 tells the worker before the meeting does, through a locked screen, which is both a poor way to be told and a poor way to run a meeting. Revoking after the meeting leaves 35 minutes of access to a customer data system for someone who is about to be terminated. The revocation is scheduled for the meeting's start time, is monitored during the interval, and any anomalous activity in the interval escalates to immediate revocation regardless of the meeting.

acceptance_criteria.given: the termination is immediate
acceptance_criteria.then: it is bound to the meeting start time rather than to the decision time or to the meeting's end

acceptance_criteria.given: activity occurs in the interval
acceptance_criteria.then: anomalous activity triggers immediate revocation regardless of the meeting

acceptance_criteria.given: the meeting starts
acceptance_criteria.then: every entitlement is revoked in one operation rather than system by system over an hour

acceptance_criteria.given: one system's revocation fails
acceptance_criteria.then: it is escalated within minutes and the system's owner is contacted directly, because a partial revocation is the exposure

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker holds a physical credential
acceptance_criteria.then: the physical and logical revocations are one plan with one completion, not two processes with separate owners

data_read.identity: the entitlements across every system and their revocation methods
data_read.people: the termination decision and its timing
data_read.security: the activity monitoring for the interval

data_written.identity: the revocation plan and its per-system outcomes
data_written.security: the interval monitoring record

authorization_and_disclosure: The revocation team receives FULL disclosure of the entitlement inventory and the timing.
The termination decision and its reason are WITHHELD from the wider IT function, which receives a revocation instruction without its basis.

failure_modes.condition: access is revoked at the decision time
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker learns they are terminated from a locked screen before anyone tells them

failure_modes.condition: revocation runs system by system over an hour
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the last system revoked is the exposure and nobody knows which one it will be

evidence_expected: The revocation plan with its scheduled time.
The interval monitoring and any escalation.
The per-system revocation outcomes with their times.

title: Delegate approval authority for a bounded period
preconditions: Tenant acme. Manager Ines Duarte delegates approval authority to a peer for 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-17.
Her authority includes pay changes up to 15,000 USD.
The peer's own authority is 8,000 USD.
story: As a manager, I want the delegation to carry my authority rather than being capped at the delegate's own, so that the delegation is useful rather than decorative
scenario: The delegate's own authority is 8,000 USD and the delegation carries 15,000 USD. Capping it at the delegate's own limit would make the delegation pointless for exactly the decisions it exists to cover. The delegated decisions are recorded as made under the delegation with both principals named, so the authority snapshot shows whose authority was used and who used it.

acceptance_criteria.given: the delegation is created
acceptance_criteria.then: it carries the delegator's authority for the stated period rather than the delegate's own

acceptance_criteria.given: the delegate approves a 12,000 USD change
acceptance_criteria.then: it names the delegate as actor and the delegator as the authority source

acceptance_criteria.given: the delegation period ends
acceptance_criteria.when: a further approval is attempted under it
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, and the delegate's own 8,000 USD authority applies instead

data_read.identity: both principals' authorities and the delegation
data_read.compensation: the proposals decided under the delegation

data_written.identity: the delegation and the approvals made under it

authorization_and_disclosure: The delegate receives FULL disclosure of the delegated scope and its period.
The delegator's other authorities outside the delegated scope are DENIED to the delegate by name.

failure_modes.condition: the delegation is capped at the delegate's own authority
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the decisions it exists to cover are exactly the ones it cannot make

failure_modes.condition: the approval names only the delegate
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the authority snapshot cannot show whose authority was exercised

evidence_expected: The delegation with its scope and period.
Each approval naming actor and authority source.
The refusal after the period ends.

title: Send an announcement to an audience that changes between drafting and sending
preconditions: Tenant acme. An announcement is drafted 2026-02-09 for 412 workers in a division.
It is sent 2026-02-13; by then the division has 418 workers and 3 have left.
Acknowledgement is tracked.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the audience to resolve at send time rather than at drafting, so that the three who left do not receive it and the six who joined do
scenario: The audience was 412 at drafting and is 415 at send: six joined and three left. Sending to the drafted list would reach three former workers and miss six current ones. The audience resolves at send, and the resolved membership is stored with the send so the acknowledgement denominator is the population that actually received it rather than the one that was drafted for.

acceptance_criteria.given: the audience is defined by rule
acceptance_criteria.then: the membership resolves at send time rather than at drafting

acceptance_criteria.given: three members left before the send
acceptance_criteria.then: they are excluded and the exclusion is recorded

acceptance_criteria.given: acknowledgement is tracked
acceptance_criteria.then: the denominator is the resolved send membership rather than the drafted list

data_read.experience: the announcement, its audience rule and the acknowledgement records
data_read.people: the division membership at send time

data_written.experience: the resolved audience, the sends and the acknowledgements

authorization_and_disclosure: Recipients receive FULL disclosure of the announcement content.
The full recipient list is DENIED to each recipient; the sender receives FULL disclosure of the resolved membership.

failure_modes.condition: the drafted list is used
failure_modes.expected_refusal: three former workers receive an internal announcement and six current ones do not

failure_modes.condition: the acknowledgement denominator is the drafted list
failure_modes.expected_refusal: completion is computed against a population that did not receive it

evidence_expected: The audience rule and its resolution at send.
The exclusions and inclusions against the draft.
The acknowledgement completion with its denominator.

title: Route an inbound message that names a matter the sender is not party to
preconditions: Tenant acme. A message arrives in the secure inbox on 2026-06-23 referencing case HR-4410.
The sender is not a party to HR-4410 and is not in its compartment.
The message is otherwise a routine query.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the routing not to confirm or deny that the referenced case exists, so that a case reference in a message is not a way to test whether a case exists
scenario: The message names a case the sender cannot see. Routing it into that case's compartment would place a non-party's message inside a wall and would confirm the case exists by where the reply comes from. The reference is stripped from the routing decision: the message is routed on its own content as a new query from this sender, and the reply neither confirms nor denies HR-4410. The reference itself is preserved on the message and surfaced to the compartment's owner, because a non-party citing a case number is worth knowing about.

acceptance_criteria.given: a message references a case the sender is not party to
acceptance_criteria.then: the reference does not affect the routing and the message is routed on its own content

acceptance_criteria.given: the reply is composed
acceptance_criteria.then: it neither confirms nor denies the referenced case, and is identical to the reply for a reference to a case that does not exist

acceptance_criteria.given: the reference is preserved
acceptance_criteria.then: they are told a non-party cited the case number, with the sender and the message identifier

acceptance_criteria.given: the sender is in fact a party whose membership was not recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the membership is corrected and the earlier non-disclosing reply stands, because it was correct on the facts as recorded

data_read.experience: the inbox, the message and the routing rules
data_read.case: the compartment membership for the referenced case

data_written.experience: the routed message and the reply
data_written.case: the notification to the compartment owner

authorization_and_disclosure: The sender receives PARTIAL disclosure: their own query is answered and the case reference is WITHHELD, with the reply identical whether or not the case exists.
The compartment owner receives FULL disclosure of the reference and the sender.

failure_modes.condition: the message is routed into the referenced compartment
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a non-party's message enters a wall and the reply's origin confirms the case exists

failure_modes.condition: the reply says the sender is not a party to that case
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the refusal confirms the case exists, which is the fact being probed

evidence_expected: The routing decision and the ignored reference.
The reply's uniformity across existing and nonexistent references.
The notification to the compartment owner.

title: A manager uses a delegation to approve a change to their own terms
preconditions: Tenant acme. Manager A delegates approval authority to Manager B for 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-18.
Manager B is Manager A's direct report and also holds a delegation from Manager A's own manager.
On 2026-09-10 a pay change for Manager B is proposed.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the delegation chain not to produce a path by which the delegate approves their own change, so that an authority loop is closed rather than being found in an audit
scenario: Manager B holds two delegations and is the subject of the proposal. The requirement resolves to Manager A's authority, which B holds by delegation, and to Manager A's manager's authority, which B also holds. Both paths route the decision to the subject. The self-approval exclusion is applied to the resolved authority rather than to the named approver, so both delegated paths are excluded and the requirement escalates past both delegators to a principal B holds no delegation from. The attempt is recorded, because a delegate approving their own terms through two chains is a pattern worth surfacing whether or not it was deliberate.

acceptance_criteria.given: a delegated authority would route a decision to its own subject
acceptance_criteria.then: the exclusion is applied to the resolved authority rather than to the named approver, so the delegated path is excluded

acceptance_criteria.given: the delegate holds two delegations that both route to them

story: As a finance partner, I want the accrual to post to the period the work belongs to rather than the period it is computed in, so that June's cost is in June

The variance between accrual and actual.

title: Add a cost centre to an org unit that already posts elsewhere

title: Escalate a case that its assignee has not touched
preconditions: Tenant acme. Case HR-5520 was assigned 2026-04-08 with a tier-2 target of five business days.

title: Attach an evidence reference rather than a document copy

title: Bridge a punch from a device whose clock is wrong
preconditions: Tenant acme. Time clock TC-14 reports a punch at 2026-05-06T08:02 local.

title: Publish a job posting whose range differs by posting location
preconditions: Tenant acme posts a remote role on 2026-03-23 open to Colorado, New York and Texas.

title: Retire a role template that positions still reference
preconditions: Tenant acme. Role template RT-140 is retired on 2026-08-10.

title: Reconcile a carrier file that arrives with yesterday's snapshot

title: Terminate a worker whose manager is the subject of their open complaint
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-170590 filed a complaint against their manager on 2026-06-02.

story: As a compliance officer, I want the termination to be routed away from the respondent manager rather than blocked outright, so that a complaint neither protects a poor performer nor licenses retaliation

title: Apply a retroactive pay change across a jurisdiction move

title: Run open enrollment while a plan's carrier contract is unsigned
preconditions: Tenant acme. Open enrollment opens 2026-11-02 for the 2027 plan year.

title: A candidate submits an application that carries instructions to the screening agent
preconditions: Tenant acme. An application arrives 2026-05-27 with white text in the resume reading as instructions to advance the candidate.

title: Add a shift swap that would breach a rest rule

title: See the org unit I sit in and its parent chain
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-170620 sits in unit U-118 on 2026-03-09.

title: Record a workplace injury that is reported three weeks late

title: Process a payroll run while a rule pack deployment is in flight
preconditions: Tenant acme. A rule pack update deploys 2026-07-01T02:00.

title: An administrator widens their own scope by editing a role definition

title: Extend a probation period once and refuse a second extension

title: Notify a carrier of a termination on the day it takes effect
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171110 terminates 2026-08-31 with coverage ending 2026-08-31.

story: As a benefits administrator, I want the termination to reach the carrier before claims are adjudicated against a closed policy, so that the worker is not billed for a September claim they thought was covered

Where the file runs later, claims incurred in the gap are adjudicated against a policy the carrier believes is active and are later reversed onto the worker. acceptance_criteria.then: the worker is notified with the coverage end date and the continuation route rather than receiving a bill without explanation

data_read.people: the termination date

data_written.integration: the termination notification
data_written.operations: the gap obligation, where one exists

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a billing surprise replaces a coverage conversation

The notification and its confirmation.

title: Refuse a time-off request that would exceed a blackout limit

title: Retire a population rule that batch actions still reference
preconditions: Tenant acme. Population rule POP-140 is retired 2026-09-07.
Three scheduled batch actions reference it.
One runs weekly.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the retirement to be blocked while scheduled actions reference the rule, so that a weekly action does not fail silently every Monday
scenario: Retiring the rule leaves three scheduled actions pointing at nothing. The weekly one would fail every Monday, and a failure that repeats on a schedule stops being noticed after the third week. Retirement is refused with the three referencing actions named, and each is either repointed or cancelled before the rule can be retired.

acceptance_criteria.given: scheduled actions reference the rule
acceptance_criteria.then: retirement is refused, the rule's BusinessState stays ACTIVE, and the referencing actions are named

acceptance_criteria.given: the actions are repointed or cancelled
acceptance_criteria.then: it succeeds and the retirement is recorded with the actions that were resolved

acceptance_criteria.given: an action is cancelled rather than repointed
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a recorded decision rather than a side effect of the retirement

data_read.population: the rule and the actions referencing it
data_read.operations: the schedules of the referencing actions

data_written.population: the refused retirement, and on resolution the retirement itself

authorization_and_disclosure: The rule's owner receives FULL disclosure of the referencing actions and their schedules.
The actions' target populations are DENIED to this operation, which reads references rather than members.

failure_modes.condition: the rule is retired with live references
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a weekly action fails every Monday and stops being noticed after three weeks

failure_modes.condition: the actions are cancelled automatically
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a scheduled action disappears as a side effect of an unrelated retirement

evidence_expected: The referencing actions and their schedules.
The refusal naming them.
The repointing or cancellation of each.

title: Resolve a case where the requester and the subject disagree on the facts
preconditions: Tenant acme. Case HR-5710 concerns an alleged missed overtime payment on 2026-03-14.
The worker says they worked 11 hours; the timecard shows 8.
The badge system shows a 10.5-hour presence.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the three sources to be presented as three sources rather than reconciled into one answer, so that the decision maker sees the disagreement rather than a conclusion somebody reached first
scenario: Three records disagree: the worker's account, the approved timecard and the badge data. Reconciling them into one number before a human looks means the reconciliation rule decides the case. All three are presented with their provenance and their known limitations, including that badge presence is not the same as time worked. The decision is a person's and the record shows what they had.

acceptance_criteria.given: three sources disagree
acceptance_criteria.when: the case is prepared for decision
acceptance_criteria.then: all three are presented with their provenance rather than being reconciled into one figure

acceptance_criteria.given: badge data is presented
acceptance_criteria.then: its limitation is stated: presence is not the same as time worked

acceptance_criteria.given: the decision is made
acceptance_criteria.then: it names which sources it relied on and why, rather than only the outcome

acceptance_criteria.given: the decision favours the worker's account
acceptance_criteria.then: the timecard is corrected through its own process with the case as its basis

data_read.case: the case and its evidence
data_read.time: the timecard, its approval and its punches
data_read.security: the badge presence records

data_written.case: the decision and its cited sources
data_written.time: any resulting timecard correction

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the three sources and the decision's reasoning.
Other workers' badge records are WITHHELD entirely, and the badge query is scoped to this worker alone.

failure_modes.condition: the sources are reconciled before a human looks
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the reconciliation rule decides the case and nobody chose that

failure_modes.condition: badge data is treated as time worked
failure_modes.expected_refusal: presence and work are conflated and the answer is wrong in both directions

evidence_expected: The three sources with their provenance.
The stated limitation on badge data.
The decision naming its relied-on sources.

title: Manage an intermittent leave whose pattern exceeds its certification
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171140 is certified for intermittent leave of up to two episodes per month.
In 2026-06 they take five episodes.
The certification permits recertification in defined circumstances.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the excess to trigger recertification rather than a denial, so that a changed condition is recertified rather than treated as abuse
scenario: Five episodes against a certified two is a significant variance and it has two possible explanations: the condition changed, or the leave is being used beyond its basis. Denying on the variance assumes the second. Recertification is requested, which is the permitted mechanism, the episodes already taken are not retroactively denied while it is outstanding, and the outcome determines the go-forward position.

acceptance_criteria.given: the usage exceeds the certified frequency
acceptance_criteria.then: recertification is requested rather than the excess being denied

acceptance_criteria.given: recertification is outstanding
acceptance_criteria.then: they are recorded and not retroactively denied while the recertification is pending

acceptance_criteria.given: the recertification supports the higher frequency
acceptance_criteria.then: the earlier episodes stand and the go-forward frequency is the certified one

acceptance_criteria.given: the recertification does not support the frequency
acceptance_criteria.then: it applies going forward, and any question about the earlier episodes is a separate matter with its own process

data_read.leave: the certification, its frequency and the episode records
data_read.documents: the certification in a protected compartment
data_read.regulatory: the recertification conditions

data_written.leave: the recertification request and the updated certification

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the recertification request and its basis.
The medical content is WITHHELD from the manager, who receives the episode dates and no frequency analysis.

failure_modes.condition: the excess is denied
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a changed condition is treated as abuse and the mechanism the rules provide is skipped

failure_modes.condition: the earlier episodes are retroactively denied
failure_modes.expected_refusal: leave already taken in good faith becomes unpaid after the fact

evidence_expected: The certification and the episode records.
The recertification request and its permitted basis.
The outcome and its forward application.

title: Reverse an access grant that was approved on a stale authority snapshot
preconditions: Tenant acme. An entitlement grant was approved 2026-05-04 by a manager whose authority ended 2026-05-01.
The approval used an authority snapshot taken 2026-04-28.
The grant is live.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the grant to be revalidated rather than revoked outright, so that an administrative gap does not remove access the worker legitimately needs
scenario: The approval rested on an authority that had ended three days earlier, because the snapshot predated the change. The approval is invalid and the grant may still be right. It is suspended rather than revoked, revalidation is requested from the current authority, and if they approve it resumes with the new approval recorded. If they do not, it is revoked with the basis named.

acceptance_criteria.given: an approval rests on a lapsed authority
acceptance_criteria.then: it is suspended and revalidation is requested from the current authority

acceptance_criteria.given: the current authority approves
acceptance_criteria.then: the grant returns to BusinessState ACTIVE, the new approval is recorded, and the original invalid approval remains in the record

acceptance_criteria.given: the current authority declines
acceptance_criteria.then: the revocation names the failed revalidation as its basis

acceptance_criteria.given: the snapshot's staleness is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: the snapshot window is itself a finding, because the same gap will produce the next invalid approval

data_read.identity: the grant, the approval and the authority snapshot
data_read.people: the approver's authority interval

data_written.identity: the suspension, the revalidation and its outcome

authorization_and_disclosure: The grant holder receives FULL disclosure of the suspension and the revalidation.
The approver's own authority change and its reason are DENIED to the holder by name.

failure_modes.condition: the grant is revoked outright
failure_modes.expected_refusal: access the worker legitimately needs is removed for an administrative gap

failure_modes.condition: the invalid approval is left standing
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an entitlement rests on an approval nobody with authority made

evidence_expected: The authority snapshot and its date against the authority interval.
The suspension and the revalidation request.
The outcome and the snapshot window finding.

title: Publish a compliance report where one control's evidence is missing
preconditions: Tenant acme produces a customer compliance report on 2026-10-19 covering 34 controls.
One control's evidence for Q3 cannot be retrieved because a log retention lapsed.
The remaining 33 have complete evidence.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the missing evidence to be reported as missing rather than the control being reported untested, so that the customer knows the difference between a gap and a failure
scenario: One control has no retrievable evidence for a quarter. Reporting it as untested is inaccurate: it was tested and the evidence has gone. Reporting it as passing is worse. The report states that the control operated with the evidence unavailable for the period, names the retention lapse as the cause, and records the lapse as its own finding, because losing evidence is a control failure of a different kind.

acceptance_criteria.given: evidence for a control cannot be retrieved
acceptance_criteria.then: the control is reported with its evidence unavailable and the cause named, rather than as untested or as passing

acceptance_criteria.given: the cause is a retention lapse
acceptance_criteria.then: the lapse is its own finding with its own remediation

acceptance_criteria.given: the customer asks about the control
acceptance_criteria.then: it distinguishes an evidence gap from a control failure and states what is known about each

acceptance_criteria.given: the evidence is later recovered
acceptance_criteria.then: the amendment supersedes the original and both remain readable with their dates

data_read.compliance: the controls, their assessments and the evidence store
data_read.provenance: the retention configuration and the lapse

data_written.compliance: the report with its evidence gap and the retention finding

authorization_and_disclosure: The customer receives FULL disclosure of the evidence gap and its cause.
The specific log contents, where any survive, are WITHHELD from the customer, who receives the assessment rather than the underlying records.

failure_modes.condition: the control is reported untested
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an inaccurate statement is made to a customer under a compliance report

failure_modes.condition: the retention lapse is not recorded as a finding
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the cause persists and the next report has the same gap

evidence_expected: The evidence gap and its period.
The retention lapse as its own finding.
The report's statement distinguishing gap from failure.

title: Reconcile a time export whose totals differ by a rounding rule
preconditions: Tenant acme. The time system reports 41,208.75 hours for 2026-05; payroll computes 41,206.50.
The difference is 2.25 hours across 1,140 workers.
The two systems round to different precisions.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the difference to be attributed to rounding rather than investigated as a data error, so that we do not spend a week on 2.25 hours
scenario: A 2.25-hour difference across 1,140 workers is roughly two thousandths of an hour each, which is the signature of a rounding difference rather than a data error. The reconciliation computes the expected rounding variance and compares the observed difference against it. Within tolerance the difference is attributed and recorded; outside it, the residual is what gets investigated, which is a much smaller and more tractable number.

acceptance_criteria.given: the two systems round differently
acceptance_criteria.then: the expected rounding variance is computed and the observed difference is compared against it

acceptance_criteria.given: the difference falls within the expected variance
acceptance_criteria.then: it is attributed to rounding with the computation recorded rather than being investigated

acceptance_criteria.given: the difference exceeds the expected variance
acceptance_criteria.then: the residual beyond the variance is what is investigated rather than the whole difference

acceptance_criteria.given: the rounding rules are changed in either system
acceptance_criteria.then: the tolerance changes with them rather than being a fixed number nobody revisits

data_read.time: the exported hours and the time system's rounding rule
data_read.payroll: the computed hours and the payroll rounding rule

data_written.payroll: the reconciliation with its attributed variance

authorization_and_disclosure: The payroll function receives FULL disclosure of both totals and the variance computation.
Individual workers' hours are DENIED to the reconciliation, which operates on totals unless a residual requires drilling in.

failure_modes.condition: the whole difference is investigated
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a week is spent on two thousandths of an hour per worker

failure_modes.condition: the difference is written off without a computed tolerance
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a real error of the same size is written off with it

evidence_expected: Both totals and both rounding rules.
The computed expected variance.
The attribution or the residual.

title: Handle a worker who transfers between tenants under a corporate divestiture
preconditions: Tenant acme divests a division to a buyer operating tenant borealis, effective 2026-12-31.
412 workers transfer with continuous service recognised by agreement.
The two tenants share no data by default.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the transfer to move the facts the buyer needs without moving the ones they have no basis for, so that the buyer gets what they contracted for and not the whole file
scenario: Four hundred and twelve workers move between two tenants that share nothing. The buyer needs enough to employ them: identity, service dates, terms, accrued balances. They have no basis for prior investigations, performance history predating the agreement or workers who did not transfer. The transfer is a defined data set agreed in the divestiture, produced as an export with its own manifest, and the sending tenant's records are retained rather than deleted, because the seller's own obligations survive the sale.

acceptance_criteria.given: workers transfer between tenants
acceptance_criteria.then: it is the set defined in the divestiture agreement rather than the full worker file

acceptance_criteria.given: prior investigations exist for a transferring worker
acceptance_criteria.then: they are WITHHELD from the transfer, and their absence is not signalled to the buyer

acceptance_criteria.given: continuous service is recognised
acceptance_criteria.then: the service date transfers and the buyer's own service-dependent entitlements compute from it

acceptance_criteria.given: the seller retains its records
acceptance_criteria.then: the seller's own obligations govern its retention rather than the transfer, so nothing is deleted because of the sale

acceptance_criteria.given: a transferred worker exercises a data subject right against the seller
acceptance_criteria.then: the seller answers for its own retained records and directs the buyer's holdings to the buyer

data_read.people: the 412 workers, their service and their terms
data_read.tenant: both tenants and the divestiture agreement's data schedule
data_read.case: any investigations, evaluated for exclusion

data_written.tenant: the transfer export with its manifest

authorization_and_disclosure: The buyer receives FULL disclosure of the agreed data set and nothing outside it.
Excluded categories are WITHHELD without signalling their existence, and non-transferring workers are WITHHELD absolutely.

failure_modes.condition: the full worker file transfers
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the buyer receives records they have no basis to hold, including investigations they were not party to

failure_modes.condition: the seller deletes its records on transfer
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the seller's own surviving obligations have no records behind them

evidence_expected: The divestiture data schedule.
The export manifest against the schedule.
The seller's retained records and their own retention basis.

title: Apply a retroactive union agreement across a closed payroll year
preconditions: Tenant acme ratifies an agreement on 2026-04-14 with wage increases retroactive to 2025-07-01.
184 covered workers are affected; 22 have since left.
The 2025 tax year is closed and reported.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the retroactive pay to be computed per worker per period and reported in the year it is paid, so that the correction is right for the leavers as well as the current workers
scenario: The increase is retroactive to a period in a closed tax year. The wages are not restated for 2025: they are paid in 2026 and reported in 2026, which is the ordinary treatment for retroactive pay. The computation runs per worker per period at the agreed rates, including for the 22 who have left, whose payments are made to their last known addresses with their own tax treatment. Skipping the leavers is the most common error and the one the union checks first.

acceptance_criteria.given: the increase is retroactive into a closed tax year
acceptance_criteria.then: the wages are reported in the year paid rather than the prior year being restated

acceptance_criteria.given: 22 covered workers have left
acceptance_criteria.then: they are included, and their payments are made with their own tax treatment and current addresses

acceptance_criteria.given: the computation runs per period
acceptance_criteria.then: each period uses the rate agreed for it rather than a single blended rate

acceptance_criteria.given: a leaver cannot be located
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the state's unclaimed property process rather than being written back

acceptance_criteria.given: the union verifies the computation
acceptance_criteria.then: it is produced per worker per period at the agreed granularity rather than as a total

data_read.labor: the agreement, its rates and its covered population
data_read.payroll: the periods, the paid wages and the leavers' records
data_read.tax: the reporting year rules for retroactive pay

data_written.payroll: the retroactive computations and the payments
data_written.operations: the unclaimed property obligations for unlocatable leavers

authorization_and_disclosure: The union receives FULL disclosure of the per-worker per-period computation at the agreed granularity.
Non-covered workers' pay is WITHHELD from the union entirely, including from any total.

failure_modes.condition: the leavers are excluded
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 22 people are owed money they are not paid, and it is the first thing the union checks

failure_modes.condition: the prior year is restated
failure_modes.expected_refusal: reported wages are amended for a payment made in the following year, which the reporting rules do not require

evidence_expected: The agreement rates by period.
The per-worker per-period computation including leavers.
The reporting year determination.

title: A worker uses a subject access request to obtain a colleague's statements
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Netherlands BV. Worker W-171150 submits an access request on 2026-09-01.
An investigation in which they are the respondent contains three colleagues' witness statements.
The statements name the requester throughout.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the statements to be assessed for third-party rights rather than disclosed because they mention the requester, so that an access right does not become a discovery tool
scenario: The statements are about the requester, which is what makes them the requester's personal data, and they are also the personal data of the colleagues who gave them. Disclosing them verbatim would identify three witnesses to the person they gave evidence about. The assessment is per document and per passage: the substance concerning the requester is disclosed, the witnesses' identities and identifying detail are withheld, and where redaction cannot protect identity the passage is withheld with the ground stated. The requester is told that content is withheld and on what basis, so they can challenge it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a document is the personal data of both the requester and a third party
acceptance_criteria.then: it is assessed per passage rather than being disclosed or withheld as a whole

acceptance_criteria.given: a witness's identity cannot be protected by redaction
acceptance_criteria.then: it is withheld with the third-party ground stated rather than being disclosed

acceptance_criteria.given: the response is issued
acceptance_criteria.then: it states that content was withheld, the ground, and the requester's right to challenge, rather than presenting a partial disclosure as complete

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester asks who gave a statement
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, and the refusal is identical whether or not that person gave one

acceptance_criteria.given: the investigation concludes and its outcome is disclosed to the requester
acceptance_criteria.then: it conveys the findings without reproducing the withheld statements, so the outcome does not undo the assessment

data_read.privacy: the request, the third-party balancing test and the response
data_read.case: the investigation, the statements and the witness identities

data_written.privacy: the per-passage assessment, the response and its stated grounds

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives PARTIAL disclosure: the substance concerning them is FULL and the withheld passages are DENIED with the third-party ground stated.
The witnesses' identities are WITHHELD absolutely, and the response's shape does not reveal how many witnesses there were.

failure_modes.condition: the statements are disclosed because they name the requester
failure_modes.expected_refusal: three witnesses are identified to the person they gave evidence about, and the next investigation gets no witnesses

failure_modes.condition: the whole investigation is withheld
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester's own personal data is refused wholesale, which the right does not permit

evidence_expected: The per-passage assessment with its grounds.
The response stating what was withheld and why.
The absence of any signal about the number of witnesses.

title: Refuse to delete a document under an active retention requirement
preconditions: Tenant acme. A deletion request covers a worker's I-9 record on 2026-06-08.
The worker terminated 2026-03-31.
The retention rule requires three years from hire or one year from termination, whichever is later.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the refusal to compute the actual disposal date rather than citing a rule, so that I know when it will be deleted rather than that it will not be
scenario: The record cannot be deleted yet and the answer worth giving is when it can. The rule is computed against the worker's own dates: hired 2024-08-12 and terminated 2026-03-31, giving a disposal date of 2027-08-12 under the three-year branch. The refusal states the computed date rather than the rule, so the requester learns something they can act on.

acceptance_criteria.given: a retention requirement blocks deletion
acceptance_criteria.then: the deletion is refused with the computed disposal date, and the record's own ObligationState carries that date rather than the request being closed

acceptance_criteria.given: the rule has two branches
acceptance_criteria.then: both branches are computed and the governing one is identified

acceptance_criteria.given: the disposal date arrives
acceptance_criteria.then: it runs without a further request, because the requirement rather than the request is what was blocking

data_read.privacy: the deletion request and the retention schedule
data_read.documents: the record and its class
data_read.people: the hire and termination dates

data_written.privacy: the refusal with its computed date

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives FULL disclosure of the computed disposal date and both branches.
The document's contents are DENIED to the requester where the requester is not the subject.

failure_modes.condition: the refusal cites the rule alone
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester learns nothing they can act on and asks again next month

failure_modes.condition: only one branch is computed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the disposal date is wrong whenever the other branch governs

evidence_expected: The hire and termination dates.
Both branch computations and the governing one.
The scheduled disposal at the computed date.

title: Approve a training budget request against a shared pool
preconditions: Tenant acme. A divisional training pool holds 84,000.00 USD for 2026 with 12,400.00 USD remaining on 2026-10-05.
Four requests totalling 18,600.00 USD are pending.
Requests are approved in submission order by policy.
story: As a finance partner, I want the pool to be reserved at approval rather than at payment, so that two approvals do not spend the same money
scenario: Four requests exceed the remaining balance. Approving on the balance and reserving at payment lets all four be approved against 12,400.00 USD, and the shortfall appears when the third one is paid. The reservation is taken at approval, so the first three approve and consume the balance and the fourth is refused with the remaining amount stated and its position in the queue.

acceptance_criteria.given: a request is approved
acceptance_criteria.then: it is taken at approval rather than at payment

acceptance_criteria.given: the pool is exhausted mid queue
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is refused, no reservation is created against the pool, and the remaining balance and its queue position are stated

acceptance_criteria.given: an approved request is later withdrawn
acceptance_criteria.then: the released amount returns to the pool and the refused request is re-evaluated

data_read.budget: the pool, its balance and the live reservations
data_read.learning: the four requests and their amounts

authorization_and_disclosure: Each requester receives FULL disclosure of their own outcome and the remaining pool balance.
Other requesters' amounts and identities are DENIED to them by name.

failure_modes.condition: the pool is reserved at payment
failure_modes.expected_refusal: four approvals are made against money for three and the shortfall appears at payment

failure_modes.condition: a withdrawn approval does not release its reservation
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the pool is permanently short by the withdrawn amount

evidence_expected: The pool balance and the reservations.
The per-request outcomes with the balance at each.
Any release and re-evaluation.

title: Detect that a worker's manager is also their subordinate
preconditions: Tenant acme. A reorganization on 2026-07-06 leaves worker A reporting to B and B reporting to A.
Approval routing traverses the management chain.
The cycle was created by two separate valid changes.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the cycle to be detected at the second change rather than by a routing failure, so that an approval does not loop forever
scenario: Each change was valid on its own and together they form a cycle. Routing an approval through this chain either loops or terminates arbitrarily, and both are worse than refusing the change. The second change is refused at commit with the cycle named and both edges shown, because the requester needs to see which pair of relationships conflicts rather than being told the hierarchy is invalid.

acceptance_criteria.given: a proposed change would create a reporting cycle
acceptance_criteria.when: the change is evaluated at commit
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with the cycle named and both edges shown

acceptance_criteria.given: the cycle already exists from a prior state
acceptance_criteria.then: it is raised as a data quality finding with both edges rather than being silently tolerated

acceptance_criteria.given: an approval is routed through a chain containing a cycle
acceptance_criteria.then: the routing terminates with ExecutionState FAILED and a typed refusal naming the cycle, rather than looping or choosing arbitrarily

acceptance_criteria.given: the cycle is broken by a further change
acceptance_criteria.then: it completes normally and the earlier refusals remain in the record

data_read.organization: the reporting relationships and the proposed change
data_read.workflow: the approval routing rules

data_written.organization: the refused change and any recorded cycle finding

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives FULL disclosure of the cycle and both edges.
The reasons behind each of the two relationships are DENIED to this operation, which reads the graph rather than the rationale.

failure_modes.condition: the cycle is tolerated
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an approval loops or terminates arbitrarily and neither is a decision

failure_modes.condition: the refusal says only that the hierarchy is invalid
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester cannot tell which pair of relationships conflicts

evidence_expected: The two edges forming the cycle.
The refusal at commit naming them.
The routing refusal, where a cycle already exists.

title: Handle a candidate who requests their assessment results
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme France SAS. Candidate C-7010 was assessed with a structured scoring instrument on 2026-05-18.
They request their results on 2026-06-02.
The instrument is licensed and its scoring key is the vendor's.
story: As a recruiter, I want the candidate's own scores to be disclosed without disclosing the vendor's scoring key, so that the right is honoured without giving away something that is not ours
scenario: The candidate's scores are their personal data and the instrument's scoring key is the vendor's intellectual property. These are separable: the scores, the dimensions they were given on and the interpretation applied to them are disclosed; the item-level weights and the normative sample are not. Refusing the whole request to protect the vendor would subordinate a right to a licence, and disclosing the key would breach the licence.

acceptance_criteria.given: the candidate requests their assessment results
acceptance_criteria.then: their scores, the dimensions and the applied interpretation are disclosed

acceptance_criteria.given: the instrument's scoring key is requested or implied
acceptance_criteria.then: the item weights and normative sample are DENIED with the licence ground stated

acceptance_criteria.given: the scores contributed to a decision
acceptance_criteria.then: the decision and the weight the scores carried in it are stated, because that is what the candidate is actually asking about

acceptance_criteria.given: the vendor asserts the scores themselves are proprietary
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused: the scores are the candidate's personal data and a licence cannot remove a data subject right

data_read.recruiting: the assessment, the scores and the decision they contributed to
data_read.privacy: the request and the balancing of rights against the licence

data_written.privacy: the disclosure with its per-element grounds

authorization_and_disclosure: The candidate receives FULL disclosure of their own scores, the dimensions and the interpretation.
The item weights and normative sample are DENIED by name with the licence ground stated, so the candidate can challenge the ground.

failure_modes.condition: the whole request is refused to protect the licence
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a data subject right is subordinated to a commercial agreement the candidate is not party to

failure_modes.condition: the scoring key is disclosed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the licence is breached and the vendor's instrument is compromised for every user

evidence_expected: The scores and their dimensions.
The disclosure with per-element grounds.
The decision and the weight the scores carried.

title: See which of my documents are still awaiting signature
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171160 has two documents awaiting their signature on 2026-03-16.
One has a deadline of 2026-03-20; the other has none.
A third document awaits a countersignature from HR.
story: As an employee, I want the documents waiting on me to be separated from those waiting on somebody else, so that I act on mine and stop worrying about the other
scenario: The view separates two documents awaiting the worker's signature from one awaiting HR's countersignature. Presenting all three as outstanding makes the worker chase a document they cannot move, and the one with a deadline is the only one that needs their attention this week.

acceptance_criteria.given: documents await different parties
acceptance_criteria.then: those awaiting the worker are separated from those awaiting others

acceptance_criteria.given: one document has a deadline
acceptance_criteria.then: the deadline is shown on that document and its absence is shown on the other

acceptance_criteria.given: the countersignature completes
acceptance_criteria.then: that document leaves the outstanding list without any action by the worker

data_read.documents: the signature requests, their parties and their deadlines

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of documents naming them as a party.
Documents in the same package that do not name them are WITHHELD; the view has no channel through which to reach them.

failure_modes.condition: all outstanding documents are shown together
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker chases a document they cannot move

title: Handle a payroll provider outage on a settlement deadline
preconditions: Tenant acme. The payroll provider is unreachable from 2026-04-14T06:00.

story: As a payroll administrator, I want the fallback to be decided against the deadline rather than after it passes, so that workers are paid on the fifteenth by some route

A decision point is set at 12:00, three hours before the deadline, which is the last moment a manual settlement can complete. At 12:00 the provider is still down and the fallback runs: a direct settlement file to the bank, computed from the same calculated run, with the provider reconciled afterwards rather than in line.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the fallback cannot complete and nobody is paid on the fifteenth

failure_modes.condition: the provider settles after the fallback

title: An approver is added to their own approval pool by a group membership change
preconditions: Tenant acme. A proposal requires approval by any member of the finance approver group.

The refusal and the recorded attempt.

title: Refuse to auto-approve a timecard with no recorded hours

title: Handle a payroll deduction ordered by two competing authorities

title: Split a bonus across two cost centres after a mid-period transfer
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171310 transferred from CC-2210 to CC-2260 on 2026-04-16.
An annual bonus of 12,000.00 USD is paid 2026-12-15 for calendar 2026.
The bonus rewards the whole year.
story: As a finance partner, I want the cost to be split by the period each centre had the worker rather than charged to the current one, so that the centre that had them for three and a half months bears its share
