Charging the whole amount to the current centre would overstate its cost by roughly 3,450.00 USD and understate the other's by the same. The split is computed by the days each centre held the position: 105 days to CC-2210 for 2026-01-01 to 2026-04-15, and 260 days to CC-2260 for 2026-04-16 to 2026-12-31, producing 3,452.05 USD and 8,547.95 USD, which sum to the bonus.

acceptance_criteria.given: the bonus period spans a cost centre transfer
acceptance_criteria.then: it is split by the days each centre held the position

acceptance_criteria.given: the split is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: they sum to the bonus and the day counts sum to the bonus period

acceptance_criteria.given: the transfer date is later corrected
acceptance_criteria.then: both centres' charges are corrected rather than only the receiving one

acceptance_criteria.given: a centre has been closed since the period
acceptance_criteria.then: its share posts to the successor centre with the mapping recorded rather than being absorbed by the open centre

data_read.compensation: the bonus, its period and its amount
data_read.budget: both cost centres and any successor mapping

data_written.budget: the split attribution across both centres

authorization_and_disclosure: Both centre owners receive FULL disclosure of their own share and the day computation.
The worker's bonus amount is DENIED to the centre owners individually where the tenant policy restricts it; the aggregate charge is disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: the whole bonus charges to the current centre
failure_modes.expected_refusal: one centre is overstated by roughly 3,500.00 USD and the other understated by the same

failure_modes.condition: a closed centre's share is absorbed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the open centre carries cost that was never its own

evidence_expected: The attribution intervals and their day counts.
The split amounts summing to the bonus.
Any successor centre mapping.

title: Handle a leave request that spans a jurisdiction change
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171320 requests leave 2026-06-01 to 2026-09-30.
They relocate from California to Texas on 2026-07-15, mid leave.
California's leave provisions differ materially from Texas's.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the entitlement to be determined by the rules that governed when the leave began rather than switching mid leave, so that my protected leave does not shorten because I moved
scenario: A leave that starts under one jurisdiction's rules and continues under another's raises a question nobody wants answered halfway through a medical absence. The entitlement is determined at the leave's start and holds for its duration, with the relocation recorded and its effect on future leaves noted. Where the destination provides a greater entitlement, the greater one applies from the relocation, because a rule that only ever reduces protection is not a rule anyone would write.

acceptance_criteria.given: a leave spans a jurisdiction change
acceptance_criteria.then: the rules at the leave's start govern its duration

acceptance_criteria.given: the destination provides a greater entitlement
acceptance_criteria.then: the greater entitlement applies from the relocation, the basis is recorded, and the leave's BusinessState is continuous across the change

acceptance_criteria.given: the relocation is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: they are evaluated under the destination's rules, so the determination is scoped to this leave

acceptance_criteria.given: the leave's payroll treatment differs by jurisdiction
acceptance_criteria.then: each period is computed under the jurisdiction in force for it, separately from the entitlement determination

data_read.leave: the request, both jurisdictions' provisions and the entitlement
data_read.people: the work location revisions and the relocation date
data_read.payroll: the periods and their jurisdictions

data_written.leave: the entitlement determination and its basis
data_written.payroll: the per-period jurisdiction treatment

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the entitlement determination and its basis.
The medical basis is WITHHELD from the manager throughout, including from the relocation record.

failure_modes.condition: the entitlement switches mid leave to the destination's rules
failure_modes.expected_refusal: protected leave shortens because the worker moved, which no jurisdiction intends

failure_modes.condition: the payroll treatment follows the entitlement determination
failure_modes.expected_refusal: wages are taxed under a state the worker no longer works in

evidence_expected: The entitlement determination and its start-date basis.
The relocation and any greater-entitlement application.
The per-period payroll jurisdiction treatment.

title: Detect a duplicate person created by two concurrent onboardings
preconditions: Tenant acme. Two onboarding processes create person records for the same human on 2026-03-16.
One comes from a recruiting conversion and one from a manual entry.
Both hold the same government identifier.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the duplicate to be blocked at creation rather than merged afterwards, so that we do not create two records and then spend a week joining them
scenario: Both records claim the same government identifier, which is the strongest available signal that they describe one person. Creating both and merging later means two employment records, two payroll enrollments and two sets of downstream effects to reconcile. The second creation is blocked with the existing record identified, and the manual entry becomes an amendment to the existing person rather than a new one.

acceptance_criteria.given: a creation claims an identifier an existing person holds
acceptance_criteria.then: the creation is blocked before any RequestState is created and the existing person is identified to the requester

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester has authority to see the existing person
acceptance_criteria.then: the existing record is identified; where they do not, the block states that a match exists without identifying it

acceptance_criteria.given: the intended change is an amendment
acceptance_criteria.then: it amends the existing person rather than creating a second record

acceptance_criteria.given: the two records were both created despite the check
acceptance_criteria.then: the merge runs with a survivor and a redirect rather than one record being deleted

data_read.people: the existing person records and their identifiers
data_read.recruiting: the conversion and its source candidate

data_written.people: the blocked creation and any amendment to the existing person

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives PARTIAL disclosure: the block is FULL and the existing person is identified only where their authority covers them, and is otherwise DENIED by name.
The government identifier itself is WITHHELD from the block message, which states that a match exists rather than reproducing the value.

failure_modes.condition: both records are created
failure_modes.expected_refusal: two employments, two payroll enrollments and two sets of downstream effects have to be reconciled

failure_modes.condition: the block reproduces the identifier
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a duplicate check becomes a way to confirm an identifier value

evidence_expected: The match and its basis.
The blocked creation.
The amendment or the merge with its redirect.

title: Withdraw a filed government return and refile it
preconditions: Tenant acme filed a quarterly return on 2026-04-30 for Q1 2026.
An error is found 2026-05-18 understating wages by 84,200.00 USD.
The authority accepts amended returns rather than withdrawals.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the correction to follow the authority's own mechanism rather than the word we use internally, so that the filing is corrected in the way the authority recognises
scenario: The internal instinct is to withdraw and refile. The authority does not accept withdrawals; it accepts amendments. The correction is filed as an amendment referencing the original, the original remains filed, and any interest and penalty on the underpayment is computed from the original due date rather than from the amendment, because that is how the authority computes it. Modelling the correction as a withdrawal would produce a reconciliation that never matches the authority's records.

acceptance_criteria.given: a filed return contains an error
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the authority's own mechanism rather than an internal notion of withdrawal

acceptance_criteria.given: the amendment is filed
acceptance_criteria.then: the original remains filed and the amendment references it

acceptance_criteria.given: interest and penalty are computed
acceptance_criteria.then: it runs from the original due date rather than from the amendment

acceptance_criteria.given: the authority's mechanism differs by jurisdiction
acceptance_criteria.then: the jurisdiction's own mechanism is used and is recorded with the filing, and the original filing's ObligationState remains SATISFIED because the amendment supplements it rather than replacing it

data_read.tax: the filed return, the authority's amendment rules and the corrected figures
data_read.payroll: the wages and deposits for the period

data_written.tax: the amended return and the computed interest and penalty

authorization_and_disclosure: The tax function receives FULL disclosure of both filings and the computed exposure.
Individual workers' wages are DENIED to this operation beyond the aggregates the return reports.

failure_modes.condition: the correction is modelled as a withdrawal
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the internal record never reconciles to the authority's, which holds both filings

failure_modes.condition: interest runs from the amendment
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the computed exposure is understated and the assessment arrives later with a different figure

evidence_expected: Both filings and their reference.
The interest computation from the original due date.
The jurisdiction's mechanism as recorded.

title: Handle a benefits open enrollment during a payroll system migration
preconditions: Tenant acme runs open enrollment 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-30 for the 2027 plan year.
The payroll system migrates 2026-12-15.
Deductions for 2027 elections must exist in the new system from the first 2027 run.
story: As a benefits administrator, I want the elections to be carried by the migration rather than re-entered after it, so that 1,802 workers' elections are not typed twice
scenario: Elections are made in November, the migration happens in December and the deductions must be live in January. Re-entering 1,802 workers' elections after the migration is a month of work and a guaranteed error rate. The elections migrate with the rest of the data, a reconciliation compares the elected tier and amount per worker on both sides, and any worker whose election does not match is held rather than being deducted on a figure nobody verified.

acceptance_criteria.given: elections are made before a migration
acceptance_criteria.then: the elections migrate with their tiers and amounts rather than being re-entered

acceptance_criteria.given: the migration completes
acceptance_criteria.then: the elected tier and amount are compared per worker on both sides, and each worker's deduction stays in ConsistencyState PENDING_OBSERVATION until its comparison passes

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker's election does not reconcile
acceptance_criteria.then: their deduction is held with the discrepancy named rather than being taken on an unverified figure

acceptance_criteria.given: an election is made after the migration cutoff but inside the window
acceptance_criteria.then: it is entered in the destination system directly rather than in the source, and the routing rule is stated to the worker

acceptance_criteria.given: the reconciliation finds a systematic difference
acceptance_criteria.then: the mapping is corrected and the whole population is re-reconciled rather than the differences being corrected individually

data_read.benefits: the elections, their tiers and amounts
data_read.payroll: both systems' deduction configurations
data_read.integration: the migration mapping

data_written.payroll: the migrated deductions and the reconciliation result
data_written.benefits: the held elections and their discrepancies

authorization_and_disclosure: Workers receive FULL disclosure of their own elections and any hold on their deduction.
The migration's technical detail is WITHHELD from workers, who are told about their own election rather than about the system change.

failure_modes.condition: elections are re-entered after the migration
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 1,802 elections are typed twice and the error rate is whatever a month of typing produces

failure_modes.condition: an unreconciled election is deducted anyway
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a worker pays a premium nobody verified against what they chose

evidence_expected: The elections before the migration.
The per-worker reconciliation on both sides.
The held deductions and their discrepancies.

title: Reverse a mass access provisioning that used a wrong role mapping
preconditions: Tenant acme. A role mapping change on 2026-07-06 provisioned an extra entitlement to 418 workers.
The entitlement grants read access to a payroll application.
It was live for nine days before detection.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the reversal to be accompanied by an assessment of what was read in those nine days, so that the access is removed and the exposure is known
scenario: Removing the entitlement from 418 workers is the easy half. The harder and more important half is that 418 people held read access to a payroll application for nine days, and the question that will be asked is what was read. The application's own access logs are queried for the affected principals in the affected window, the count and nature of reads are established, and any read of another worker's compensation is treated as a disclosure with its own assessment.

acceptance_criteria.given: an entitlement was provisioned in error
acceptance_criteria.then: the entitlement is removed from all 418 and the removal is confirmed per principal

acceptance_criteria.given: the entitlement was live for nine days
acceptance_criteria.then: the target application's access logs are queried for the affected principals in the affected window

acceptance_criteria.given: reads occurred
acceptance_criteria.then: each read of another worker's compensation is treated as a disclosure with its own assessment rather than being counted

acceptance_criteria.given: the target application has no access logs
acceptance_criteria.then: the absence is itself a finding and the exposure is recorded as undetermined rather than as none

acceptance_criteria.given: the mapping change is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: the absence of an impact preview before the mapping change is the finding rather than the mapping itself

data_read.identity: the role mapping, the provisioned entitlements and the 418 principals
data_read.security: the target application's access logs for the window
data_read.compensation: the records reachable through the entitlement

data_written.security: the exposure assessment and any disclosure findings

authorization_and_disclosure: The security function receives FULL disclosure of the access logs for the affected window.

The 418 workers are notified only where their own access is being removed; the exposure assessment is WITHHELD from them, and any worker whose compensation was read receives FULL disclosure of that read.

failure_modes.condition: the entitlement is removed and the matter closed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 418 people held payroll read access for nine days and nobody asked what was read

failure_modes.condition: missing logs are treated as no exposure
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an absence of evidence is recorded as evidence of absence

evidence_expected: The mapping change and the provisioned set.
The per-principal removal confirmations.
The access log assessment and any disclosure findings.

title: A former worker's session token is used after their termination
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171330 terminated 2026-06-30T17:00 with entitlements revoked at 17:00.
A session token issued at 16:20 is presented at 17:14.
The token's own expiry is 18:20.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the token to be rejected on the principal's state rather than on its own expiry, so that revocation means revoked rather than expiring within two hours
scenario: The token is unexpired and was validly issued. Its bearer no longer holds the entitlements it was issued against, and a token that outlives its principal's authority is a two-hour window in which a revocation has not happened. The presentation is refused on the principal's current state, which is checked at each use rather than being baked into the token. The use is recorded as a post-revocation presentation, because a token presented fourteen minutes after a revocation is worth distinguishing from an ordinary expiry.

acceptance_criteria.given: a token is presented after its principal's entitlements are revoked
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused on the principal's current entitlement state rather than on the token's expiry, and no session RequestState is established

acceptance_criteria.given: the token is unexpired
acceptance_criteria.then: the unexpired token does not override the revocation, because authority is checked at use

acceptance_criteria.given: the presentation is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded as a post-revocation presentation with both timestamps rather than as an ordinary expiry

acceptance_criteria.given: the same token is presented repeatedly
acceptance_criteria.then: the repetition escalates and each individual refusal remains identical

acceptance_criteria.given: the revocation had not completed in one system
acceptance_criteria.then: the incomplete revocation is a finding, because the control is the revocation rather than the token

data_read.security: the token, its issuance and expiry, and the principal's entitlement state
data_read.people: the termination and its effective time
data_read.identity: the revocation records and their completion times

data_written.security: the refusal and the recorded post-revocation presentation

authorization_and_disclosure: The presenter receives the typed authority refusal; whether the principal exists is WITHHELD from the refusal.
The security function receives FULL disclosure of the presentation, both timestamps and the revocation completion times.

failure_modes.condition: the token is honoured until its own expiry
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a revocation takes effect up to two hours after it is made

failure_modes.condition: the presentation is logged as an ordinary expiry
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a post-revocation attempt is indistinguishable from a session timing out

evidence_expected: The token's issuance and expiry against the revocation time.
The refusal on principal state.
The recorded post-revocation presentation and any repetition.

title: Refuse a case reassignment that would breach a conflict wall
preconditions: Tenant acme. Case HR-5910 concerns a dispute between two workers.
A supervisor reassigns it 2026-07-27 to a partner who is one worker's spouse.

story: As an HR business partner, I want the conflict register to be checked at assignment rather than relied on being remembered, so that the assignment is refused by a check rather than by someone happening to know
scenario: The relationship is recorded and the supervisor does not know it. Relying on human recollection means the wall holds only when the right person is in the room. The assignment is refused against the register with the conflict class named and not the relationship itself, so the supervisor learns that a conflict exists without learning that two colleagues are married.

acceptance_criteria.given: an assignment would create a registered conflict
acceptance_criteria.then: the assignment is refused, the case's own assignment is unchanged, and the conflict class is named

acceptance_criteria.given: the refusal is issued
acceptance_criteria.then: the underlying relationship is WITHHELD and only the conflict class is disclosed

data_read.people: the relationship, read by the check and not disclosed

data_written.case: the refused assignment and the escalation

The parties to the case are not told that an assignment was attempted and refused.

failure_modes.condition: the register is consulted by memory
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the wall holds only when the right person is in the room

failure_modes.condition: the refusal names the relationship
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a routing check discloses a personal relationship to a supervisor who had no need to know it

The refusal naming the class alone.
The escalated assignment.

title: Apply a currency change to a worker paid in a non-functional currency
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171340 is employed by Acme UK and paid in GBP.
Their salary is expressed in GBP and reported to the group in USD.
A 4 percent increase is approved 2026-05-11.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the increase to be applied in the currency of the contract rather than in the reporting currency, so that my raise is four percent rather than four percent minus an exchange movement

Applying the increase to the USD figure and converting back would give the worker four percent adjusted by whatever the rate has done since, which is not a raise anybody agreed. The increase applies to the GBP amount, the USD figure is a derived reporting value, and the derivation carries its rate and date.

acceptance_criteria.given: the contract currency differs from the reporting currency
acceptance_criteria.then: it applies to the contract currency amount, and the increase reaches BusinessState EFFECTIVE on its own date regardless of any rate movement

acceptance_criteria.given: the reporting figure is produced

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of their contract currency amount and the increase applied to it.
The group reporting conversion is DENIED to the worker as immaterial to their terms, and is disclosed on request.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker's raise is four percent adjusted by an exchange movement they did not agree to

failure_modes.condition: the reporting figure is stored as a stated amount
failure_modes.expected_refusal: it stops tracking the contract amount and the two diverge silently

The derived reporting figure with its rate and date.
The approval bound to the contract currency amount.

title: Record a manager's decision not to act on a performance concern
preconditions: Tenant acme. A manager raises a performance concern in a 2026-04-14 check-in.
They decide not to open a formal process.
The concern is real and the decision is deliberate.
story: As a manager, I want the decision not to act to be recordable rather than only actions being recorded, so that a deliberate choice is distinguishable from inattention
scenario: A record that only holds actions cannot distinguish a manager who considered a concern and decided it did not warrant a formal process from one who never noticed. acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded with its basis and a review date

data_read.people: the worker and the reporting relationship

The decision with its basis and review date.
The prompted review.

title: Handle a subject access request that spans a former employer's records
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. A request arrives 2026-08-10 from a worker transferred in under a business transfer in 2024.

acceptance_criteria.given: the tenant holds records received from a transferor

failure_modes.condition: the transfer agreement is treated as limiting the access right

title: Detect a payroll figure that changed with no corresponding intent
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171350's base rate changed from 84,000.00 to 86,520.00 USD effective 2026-05-01.

acceptance_criteria.given: a revision has no originating intent

data_read.compensation: the rate revisions and any intents

title: Handle a works council objection to a new processing
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. A new productivity analytics processing is proposed for 2026-10-01.

failure_modes.condition: the employer decides unilaterally when agreement fails
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the conciliation mechanism exists precisely for that case

The objection and its recorded grounds.
The agreement or the conciliation referral.

title: Correct a year-end statement after it was issued to workers
preconditions: Tenant acme issued year-end statements to 1,802 workers on 2027-01-28.
An error in imputed income affects 214 of them.
The average understatement is 340.00 USD.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the correction to reach the workers and the authority through their own mechanisms, so that a worker who has already filed knows they need to act
scenario: Statements were issued and some workers will have filed on them. Correcting the internal record and the authority filing is necessary and insufficient: 214 people hold a document they may have relied on. acceptance_criteria.given: a worker may have filed on the original

acceptance_criteria.given: the authority correction is filed
acceptance_criteria.then: the corrected statement figures and the corrected filing figures match

acceptance_criteria.given: the unaffected 1,588 workers are considered
acceptance_criteria.then: they receive nothing, because their statements are correct and a general notice would create confusion

The cause of the error is DENIED to the workers where it names another person's action, and the affected population's identity is WITHHELD from the unaffected workers.

failure_modes.condition: only the authority filing is corrected
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 214 people hold a document they may have relied on and do not know it was wrong

failure_modes.condition: a general notice goes to all 1,802
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 1,588 workers are told to check a statement that is correct

The corrected authority filing and its reconciliation.
The delivery of the corrected statements to the 214.

title: Apply a collective agreement that changes retroactively during a payroll year
preconditions: Tenant acme. An agreement ratified 2026-09-14 changes shift differentials retroactive to 2026-01-01.
The differential rises from 1.50 to 2.10 USD per hour.
128 covered workers worked differential-eligible hours in the period.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the retroactive differential to be computed from the recorded hours rather than estimated, so that each worker is paid for the hours they actually worked at the new rate
scenario: The differential rises by 0.60 USD per hour retroactive to January. Estimating from an average would be quick and would be wrong for every worker individually. The recomputation runs from the recorded differential-eligible hours per worker per period, which the time records already hold. Overtime computed on a regular rate that included the differential is also recomputed, because a differential increase changes the regular rate and therefore the overtime premium.

acceptance_criteria.given: the differential changes retroactively
acceptance_criteria.then: it runs from the recorded differential-eligible hours per worker per period

acceptance_criteria.given: overtime was worked in the period
acceptance_criteria.then: the regular rate is recomputed with the new differential and the overtime premium follows

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker's hours are disputed
acceptance_criteria.then: the undisputed periods are paid and the disputed periods are held with the dispute recorded

acceptance_criteria.given: a covered worker has left
acceptance_criteria.then: they are included and paid at their last known address

acceptance_criteria.given: the union verifies the computation
acceptance_criteria.then: it is produced per worker per period with the eligible hours shown rather than as a total

data_read.labor: the agreement, the differential rates and the covered population
data_read.time: the differential-eligible hours per worker per period
data_read.payroll: the paid periods and the overtime computations

data_written.payroll: the recomputed differentials and overtime premiums

authorization_and_disclosure: The union receives FULL disclosure of the per-worker per-period computation including the eligible hours.
Non-covered workers' hours and pay are WITHHELD from the union entirely.

failure_modes.condition: the retro is estimated from an average
failure_modes.expected_refusal: it is wrong for every worker individually and the union recomputes it anyway

failure_modes.condition: the overtime premium is not recomputed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a differential increase changes the regular rate and the overtime owed is understated

evidence_expected: The agreement rates and their retroactive date.
The per-worker per-period eligible hours.
The recomputed differentials and overtime premiums.

title: See the effective date range a benefit election covers
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171360 made a mid-year election on 2026-04-06 after a qualifying event.
It takes effect 2026-05-01 and runs to the plan year end.
Their prior election ran to 2026-04-30.
story: As an employee, I want the two elections to show contiguous intervals rather than one replacing the other, so that I can see that no day is uncovered
scenario: The view shows the prior election running to 2026-04-30 and the new one from 2026-05-01, which is what tells the worker there is no uncovered day. An election that simply replaces another shows only the current one, and a gap between them is invisible until a claim is denied.

acceptance_criteria.given: two elections exist in a plan year
acceptance_criteria.then: each shows its own interval and the intervals are contiguous

acceptance_criteria.given: a gap exists between two elections

acceptance_criteria.given: the new election supersedes the prior one

data_read.benefits: the elections, their intervals and the plan year

The qualifying event's supporting documentation is FULL to the worker and DENIED to their manager.

failure_modes.condition: only the current election is shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a gap between elections is invisible until a claim is denied

failure_modes.condition: the intervals are rendered as a single continuous coverage
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a real gap is presented as continuous coverage

evidence_expected: Both elections with their intervals.
The qualifying event and its date.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Read the state of a bulk import I submitted
preconditions: Tenant acme. A 320-row import was submitted 2026-03-02 and is validating.
208 rows have validated and 108 are pending.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the submitter waits to start work they could have started

The counts by state.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Check which jurisdiction's rules a computation used
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171370's 2026-05-15 pay computed withholding for two states.

The reciprocity position at the computation's date.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Look up which workflow instance is handling my request

title: See which of my data a report included
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Ireland Ltd. Worker W-171390 asks which reports include their data on 2026-07-13.

acceptance_criteria.given: a report suppresses the worker's cell

The suppression noted where it applies.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Refuse a name change that would break an active government filing
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171400 requests a legal name change effective 2026-01-31, backdated.

title: Handle an approval that arrives after the proposal was withdrawn
preconditions: Tenant acme. A proposal was withdrawn by its author on 2026-05-04 at 11:00.

title: Record a garnishment release from the issuing authority

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker funds the delay in a recovery between two other parties

title: Refuse a knowledge answer that would require reading a case
preconditions: Tenant acme. A worker asks an assistant on 2026-04-27 what is happening with their open case.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: it looks responsive and tells the worker nothing about their situation

failure_modes.expected_refusal: it is answering from a capability it does not hold

title: Add a required field to a form without invalidating drafts

title: Handle a survey response submitted after the window closes

title: Record an offer negotiation round without overwriting the prior terms

title: Suppress a duplicate notification for one underlying event
preconditions: Tenant acme. A pay change for worker W-171430 triggers notifications from three subsystems on 2026-06-01.

title: Refuse to enroll a worker in a plan their entity does not offer
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171440 is employed by Acme Services.

title: Reconcile a payroll where a currency devalues mid period
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Argentina SA. Salaries are set in local currency and a subset carry a foreign-currency reference.

The index value and window recorded per computation.
The true-up obligation, where an estimate was used.

The recorded request scope and the process finding.

title: Compute overtime where two definitions of the workweek collide
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171700 in California works 9 hours on four days and 4 hours on a fifth, totalling 40.

Both computations run, the results are compared and the more favourable to the worker governs, with both figures recorded so the comparison is checkable.

acceptance_criteria.then: each day is computed under the rule in force at the place the work was performed

data_read.regulatory: the federal and state overtime rules
data_read.payroll: the regular rate and the premium computation

The double-count exclusion.

The unchanged employment terms.

title: Handle a candidate who withdraws consent for their data mid process

title: Restore service after a cell failure with partially replicated state

title: Suppress a notification during a declared incident
preconditions: Tenant acme. An incident on 2026-07-21 causes 4,200 spurious obligation breach notifications.

The suppression is scoped to the class rather than to all notifications.

authorization_and_disclosure: Operations receives FULL disclosure of the suppression, its scope and the re-evaluation.

title: Record an evidence artifact that is too large to store inline
preconditions: Tenant acme. An evidence artifact for a 2026-09 assessment is a 2.4 GB log archive.

story: As an auditor, I want the reference to carry enough to retrieve and verify the artifact rather than only pointing at it, so that the evidence is still verifiable in three years

title: Correct a classification that changes an entire population's overtime status
preconditions: Tenant acme. 148 workers in a job family were classified exempt from overtime.

scenario: One hundred and forty-eight workers were treated as exempt and were not. The exposure is the overtime each of them worked in each week of the affected period, which the time records hold for those who recorded time and do not hold for those who did not, because exempt workers often are not required to. Where records exist the computation is exact; where they do not, a reconstruction is made from schedules and other evidence with its basis recorded, and the two categories are reported separately rather than blended into one figure.

acceptance_criteria.given: no time records exist for a worker
acceptance_criteria.then: it is reconstructed with its basis recorded and reported separately from the exact figures

acceptance_criteria.given: the correction is applied going forward
acceptance_criteria.then: the workers begin recording time and the forward position is separate from the historical exposure

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker's exposure crosses a statute of limitations boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: the period is bounded by the applicable limitation and the boundary is recorded rather than the whole period being computed or the whole claim being assumed barred

data_read.people: the 148 workers and their duties

data_written.time: the forward classification change
data_written.payroll: the per-worker exposure and any payments

The employer's aggregate exposure and its legal analysis are DENIED to the workers and are privileged.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the figure is an approximation and each worker is paid a share of an estimate rather than what they are owed

failure_modes.condition: reconstructed and exact figures are blended
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the reliability of the whole figure is that of its weakest part and nobody can tell which parts those are

evidence_expected: The duties test conclusion and its basis.
The per-worker per-week computation, exact and reconstructed separately.
The limitation boundary and the forward classification change.

title: A support engineer reads a tenant through a shared analytics dataset
preconditions: Tenant acme. A platform analytics dataset aggregates operational metrics across tenants.

story: As a compliance officer, I want the dataset to refuse a query whose result set is attributable to one tenant, so that aggregation is not anonymisation when the filter can be narrowed to one
scenario: The dataset holds aggregates and its protection is that no row is about a tenant. A filter narrow enough to isolate one tenant defeats that: the aggregate becomes a report about acme, computed from acme's data, read by somebody with no grant to acme. The query is refused on the result set's attributability rather than on the filter's shape, because a filter can be written many ways and the property that matters is whether the answer is about one tenant. The attempt is recorded and surfaced.

acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused on the attributability of the result rather than on the filter's shape

acceptance_criteria.given: the query is rewritten to reach the same result differently
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused identically, because the check is on the result rather than on the syntax

acceptance_criteria.given: the result set spans enough tenants to be non-attributable
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns, and the threshold applied is recorded with the result

acceptance_criteria.given: the attempt is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it records the query, the attributability determination and the caller, and is surfaced to platform security

acceptance_criteria.given: the engineer holds a support grant to that tenant
acceptance_criteria.then: it is still refused through this dataset, because the grant authorizes access through the tenant's own surfaces rather than through a platform aggregate

data_read.identity: the caller's platform role and any tenant grants
data_read.security: the query history for the caller

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a rewritten filter reaches the same result and the check is defeated by syntax

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a grant scoped to a tenant's surfaces becomes a grant to every dataset that contains that tenant

evidence_expected: The attributability determination and its threshold.
The refusal and its uniformity across rewrites.
The recorded attempt surfaced to platform security.

title: Record a phased return to work with changing hours
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-171960 returns from a workers compensation absence on 2026-07-06.

title: Detect a connector writing data no mapping declares
preconditions: Tenant acme. A connector's declared mapping covers 14 fields.

story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the undeclared fields to be blocked rather than logged, so that the declaration is the contract rather than a description

title: Handle a grievance about a decision made by an automated rule
preconditions: Tenant acme. A shift assignment was made by an automated seniority rule on 2026-06-08.

title: A principal replays an approval by resubmitting an unchanged proposal

The 212 transfer to the buyer on 2026-12-01.
story: As a payroll administrator, I want the run to cover the 212 through their last day under acme rather than excluding them early, so that workers who are ours until Monday are paid by us for the period we employed them
scenario: The workers transfer on 2026-12-01 and the run covers a period ending 2026-11-30, during which they were acme's. Excluding them from the run because the divestiture is imminent would leave them unpaid for time they worked for acme. They are included through 2026-11-30, their final acme positions are computed including any termination-triggered entitlements the transfer does or does not attract, and the buyer's own payroll starts from 2026-12-01 with no overlap.

acceptance_criteria.given: workers transfer the day after a period ends
acceptance_criteria.then: they are included through their last day under the transferring employer

acceptance_criteria.given: the transfer is a business transfer rather than a termination
acceptance_criteria.then: termination-triggered entitlements are assessed against the transfer's own character rather than being triggered by default

acceptance_criteria.given: the buyer's payroll begins
acceptance_criteria.then: it begins 2026-12-01 with no day covered by both employers

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker's final acme payment settles after the transfer
acceptance_criteria.then: it is made by acme for the period acme employed them, regardless of who employs them when it settles

acceptance_criteria.given: the transfer date moves
acceptance_criteria.then: the population and the boundary move with it rather than the run being executed on the original assumption

data_read.people: the 212 workers, the transfer and its character
data_read.payroll: the period, the run and the accumulators
data_read.regulatory: the transfer's effect on termination-triggered entitlements

data_written.payroll: the run including the 212 through 2026-11-30

authorization_and_disclosure: The 212 workers receive FULL disclosure of which employer pays which period and their final acme positions.
The divestiture's commercial terms are DENIED to the workers; the transfer's effect on their employment is disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: the 212 are excluded from the run
failure_modes.expected_refusal: workers are unpaid for time they worked for the transferring employer

failure_modes.condition: termination entitlements are triggered by default
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a business transfer is treated as a termination and 212 settlements are made that the transfer's character may not require

evidence_expected: The transfer date and the period boundary.
The run covering the 212 through their last day.
The entitlement assessment against the transfer's character.

title: Reconstruct an intent's decision path after a definition was deleted
preconditions: Tenant acme. An intent committed 2025-08-14 under a workflow definition version since deleted.
The audit asks how the decision was routed.
The instance's step history survives.
story: As an auditor, I want the path to be reconstructible from the instance rather than from the definition, so that the audit does not depend on a definition somebody was allowed to delete
scenario: The definition is gone and the instance's own step history is not. An audit that depends on the definition to explain an instance is an audit that fails whenever a definition is deleted, which somebody was permitted to do. The instance records each step it executed, the decision made at each and the version it was bound to, so the path is reconstructible from the instance alone. The definition's deletion is separately a finding, because deleting a version that instances reference should not have been permitted.

acceptance_criteria.given: a definition version is deleted
acceptance_criteria.when: an instance bound to it is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: its step history reconstructs the path without the definition

acceptance_criteria.given: each step is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: the decision made at it and the version it was bound to are both present

acceptance_criteria.given: the deletion is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: deleting a version that instances reference is itself a finding rather than a fact the audit works around

acceptance_criteria.given: a step's decision depended on a rule table also deleted
acceptance_criteria.then: the decision and its inputs are present on the step and the missing table is recorded as a gap in the explanation rather than in the path

acceptance_criteria.given: other instances are bound to the same deleted version
acceptance_criteria.then: they are enumerated by their binding, so the finding covers every instance the deletion touched rather than the one the audit happened to reach

data_read.workflow: the instance, its step history and the deleted definition
data_read.provenance: the decisions recorded at each step

data_written.provenance: the reconstructed path and the deletion finding

authorization_and_disclosure: The auditor receives FULL disclosure of the step history and the reconstructed path.
The instance's subject data is DENIED to the auditor beyond what their mandate covers, and the path is reconstructible without it.

failure_modes.condition: the audit depends on the definition
failure_modes.expected_refusal: it fails whenever a definition is deleted and somebody was permitted to delete it

failure_modes.condition: the deletion is worked around without a finding
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the next definition is deleted too

evidence_expected: The instance step history with its decisions.
The reconstructed path.
The deletion recorded as a finding.

title: Handle a benefits claim under a plan the employer no longer administers
preconditions: Tenant acme moved its administration to a new provider on 2026-07-01.
A claim for a 2026-03 service is submitted 2026-09-14.
The prior administrator holds the adjudication records for that period.
story: As a benefits administrator, I want the claim to be routed to the administrator that holds the period rather than to the current one, so that the claim is adjudicated by whoever holds the records it depends on
scenario: The claim is for a period the current administrator never administered, and adjudicating it there means adjudicating without the accumulators, the prior claims and the plan configuration that governed the period. The claim routes to the prior administrator under the runout arrangement, the routing is transparent to the worker rather than requiring them to know which administrator to approach, and where the runout arrangement has ended the claim is escalated rather than being adjudicated on incomplete data.

acceptance_criteria.given: a claim covers a period administered by a prior provider
acceptance_criteria.then: it goes to the administrator that holds the period's records

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker submits it
acceptance_criteria.then: it is transparent to the worker rather than requiring them to know which administrator to approach

acceptance_criteria.given: the runout arrangement has ended
acceptance_criteria.then: it is escalated rather than adjudicated on incomplete data

acceptance_criteria.given: the prior administrator's decision is appealed
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the arrangement in force for the period rather than the current provider's appeal process

acceptance_criteria.given: the accumulators for the period are needed by the current administrator
acceptance_criteria.then: the transfer is a defined operation with its own record rather than the current administrator estimating them

data_read.benefits: the plan, both administration arrangements and the runout terms
data_read.integration: both administrators' connectors and the period boundaries

data_written.benefits: the routed claim and its adjudication route

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of which administrator handles their claim and the appeal route.
The commercial terms of either administration arrangement are DENIED to the worker.

failure_modes.condition: the claim is adjudicated by the current administrator
failure_modes.expected_refusal: it is adjudicated without the accumulators and prior claims that govern it

failure_modes.condition: the worker is told to approach the prior administrator themselves
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the employer's arrangement becomes the worker's navigation problem

evidence_expected: The period boundary and the administration arrangements.
The routed claim and its adjudication.
The appeal route for the period.

title: A batch action is approved on a preview that reads a different population
preconditions: Tenant acme. A bulk termination action is previewed on 2026-11-30 showing 12 workers.
The approval is given against the preview.
The execution reads the population live and returns 340.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the approval to bind the preview's own result rather than the query that produced it, so that the approver approved twelve names
scenario: The preview showed twelve and the execution reads live and finds 340. Whether the difference came from a rule edit, a data change or a deliberate act, an approval given against a preview must bind what the approver saw. The preview's result is captured with a digest, the approval binds that digest, and the execution refuses when the live population's digest differs. The refusal names both counts, and where the difference is this large the attempt is surfaced to compliance regardless of its cause.

acceptance_criteria.given: an approval is given against a preview
acceptance_criteria.then: it binds the digest of the preview's own result rather than the query

acceptance_criteria.given: the execution reads a different population
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused on the digest mismatch and both counts are named

acceptance_criteria.given: the difference is large
acceptance_criteria.then: it is surfaced to compliance regardless of its cause, because a twelve-to-340 difference is worth a look either way

acceptance_criteria.given: the population legitimately changed between preview and execution
acceptance_criteria.then: a fresh preview and a fresh approval are required rather than the existing approval being reused

acceptance_criteria.given: the preview and the execution match
acceptance_criteria.then: it covers exactly the approved membership and the digest match is recorded

data_read.population: the preview result, its digest and the live evaluation
data_read.workflow: the approval and the digest it binds
data_read.people: the workers in both populations

data_written.workflow: the refused execution and the recorded attempt

authorization_and_disclosure: The approver receives FULL disclosure of both counts and the digest mismatch.
The 328 additional workers are WITHHELD from the refusal, which names the count rather than the membership.

failure_modes.condition: the approval binds the query
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an approver who reviewed twelve names authorizes an action against 340

failure_modes.condition: a large difference is treated as an ordinary mismatch
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the one case most likely to be deliberate is handled as a routine refusal

evidence_expected: The preview result and its digest.
The approval binding and the live evaluation's digest.
The refusal and the surfaced attempt.

title: A worker's own access request is used to extract a colleague's assessment
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Ireland Ltd. Worker W-172370 requests access to their own performance records on 2026-05-11.
The records include a calibration discussion comparing them to four named colleagues.
The comparison is the requester's personal data and the colleagues' too.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the comparative content to be assessed rather than disclosed because the requester appears in it, so that an access right does not reach four other people's assessments
scenario: The calibration discussion is about the requester, which makes it their personal data, and it is equally about four colleagues. Disclosing it because the requester appears in it hands them four colleagues' assessments. The assessment is per passage: what concerns the requester is disclosed, the colleagues' names and their own assessments are withheld, and where the comparison cannot be conveyed without identifying a colleague's position the passage is withheld with the ground stated so the requester can challenge it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a record is the personal data of the requester and of third parties
acceptance_criteria.then: it is assessed per passage rather than disclosed or withheld as a whole

acceptance_criteria.given: a comparison cannot be conveyed without identifying a colleague's position
acceptance_criteria.then: it is withheld with the third-party ground stated rather than being disclosed

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester asks who they were compared against
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, and the refusal is identical whether or not a given colleague was in the cohort

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester's own rating and its basis are separable
acceptance_criteria.then: they are disclosed in full, because the third-party ground does not extend to the requester's own outcome

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester challenges a withholding
acceptance_criteria.then: the ground is stated specifically enough to be challenged and the supervisory authority route is included

data_read.privacy: the request, the third-party balancing and the response
data_read.talent: the calibration discussion, the ratings and the cohort

data_written.privacy: the per-passage assessment and the response with its grounds

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives PARTIAL disclosure: their own rating and its basis are FULL and the comparative passages are DENIED with the ground stated.
The four colleagues' identities and assessments are WITHHELD absolutely, and the response's shape does not reveal the cohort's size.

failure_modes.condition: the discussion is disclosed because the requester appears in it
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an access right hands the requester four colleagues' assessments

failure_modes.condition: the whole record is withheld
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester's own rating and its basis are refused, which the right does not permit

evidence_expected: The per-passage assessment with its grounds.
The requester's own rating disclosed in full.
The response's uniformity as to the cohort's size.

title: A connector is reconfigured to point at an endpoint the assessment never covered
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. A connector's transfer assessment covers an endpoint in Ireland.
On 2026-12-07 its endpoint configuration is changed to a host outside the EU.
The editor holds connector configuration authority.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the endpoint to be bound to the assessment rather than being a configuration value, so that an assessment about a destination is not satisfied by a different destination
scenario: The assessment examined a specific destination and the configuration change points the connector somewhere else. If the endpoint is an ordinary configuration value, the assessment is about a place the data no longer goes and nobody notices. The endpoint is bound to the assessment: a change to it invalidates the assessment and is refused until a new one covers the new destination. The attempt is recorded with both endpoints and their countries, because a change from an EU host to one outside it is worth distinguishing from a change between two hosts in the same country.

acceptance_criteria.given: a connector's endpoint is changed
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused unless a transfer assessment covers the new destination

acceptance_criteria.given: the new destination is outside the assessed region
acceptance_criteria.then: both endpoints and their countries are recorded and the attempt is surfaced to the privacy function

acceptance_criteria.given: a new assessment covers the destination
acceptance_criteria.then: the connector's endpoint and its assessment are rebound together

acceptance_criteria.given: the change is between two hosts within the assessed region
acceptance_criteria.then: the assessment's own scope decides, and a scope stated by country permits it while a scope stated by host does not

acceptance_criteria.given: the connector is already transmitting when the change is attempted
acceptance_criteria.then: the in-flight transmissions continue to the assessed endpoint rather than being redirected mid operation

data_read.integration: the connector, its endpoint and its assessment binding
data_read.privacy: the transfer assessment, its scope and the destination countries

data_written.integration: the refused change
data_written.privacy: the recorded attempt with both endpoints

authorization_and_disclosure: The editor receives FULL disclosure of the refusal, the assessment's scope and the route to a new assessment.
The privacy function's own risk analysis of the new destination is WITHHELD from the editor until the assessment concludes.

failure_modes.condition: the endpoint is an ordinary configuration value
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the assessment describes a destination the data no longer goes to and nobody notices

failure_modes.condition: the change is permitted pending a new assessment
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the transfer happens first and the assessment describes it afterwards

evidence_expected: The assessment and its endpoint binding.
The refused change with both endpoints and countries.
The recorded attempt surfaced to the privacy function.

title: Record a worker's declaration of an outside interest
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172380 declares a directorship in an unrelated company on 2026-03-09.
The policy requires declaration rather than approval.
The interest creates no conflict with their role.
story: As an employee, I want the declaration to be recorded and assessed rather than approved, so that declaring is not asking permission
scenario: The policy requires declaration and the worker has declared. Treating it as an approval request implies the employer may refuse an outside interest it has no basis to refuse, and workers who expect a refusal stop declaring. The declaration is recorded, assessed for conflict, and the assessment's outcome is disclosed to the worker. Where a conflict is found, the conversation that follows is about managing it rather than about permission that was never sought.

acceptance_criteria.given: a declaration is made under a declare-only policy
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded and assessed rather than routed for approval

acceptance_criteria.given: the assessment finds no conflict
acceptance_criteria.then: it is disclosed to the worker rather than the declaration disappearing into a register

acceptance_criteria.given: the assessment finds a conflict
acceptance_criteria.then: the conversation is about managing the conflict rather than about permission

data_read.compliance: the declaration policy, the register and the conflict criteria
data_read.people: the worker's role and its exposures

data_written.compliance: the declaration and its assessment outcome

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the assessment outcome and any management measures.
The register's other entries are DENIED to the worker by name.

failure_modes.condition: the declaration is routed for approval
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the employer implies a power to refuse it has no basis for and workers stop declaring

failure_modes.condition: the declaration disappears into a register
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker does not know whether it was assessed and the next one is not made

evidence_expected: The declaration and its date.
The assessment against the conflict criteria.
The outcome disclosed to the worker.

title: See the accrual rate that applies to me now
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172390 reaches five years of service on 2026-07-14.
The accrual rate steps at five years.
They check on 2026-06-30.
story: As an employee, I want the current rate and the next step with its date to be shown together, so that I can plan around a rate change I know is coming
scenario: The rate steps in two weeks and a view showing only the current rate makes the change look like an error when it happens. The current rate, the next step and the date it takes effect are shown together, so the worker sees a schedule rather than a number that will move.

acceptance_criteria.given: a rate step is approaching
acceptance_criteria.then: the current rate, the next rate and the step date are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: the step passes
acceptance_criteria.then: the new rate applies and the prior rate remains readable with its interval

acceptance_criteria.given: no further step exists
acceptance_criteria.then: that is stated rather than the next-step section being absent

data_read.leave: the accrual schedule, the service computation and the current rate

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of their own rate schedule and service computation.
Colleagues' rates and service are WITHHELD; the view has no channel through which to request them.

failure_modes.condition: only the current rate is shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the step looks like an error when it happens

failure_modes.condition: the next-step section is absent at the top of the schedule
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker cannot tell whether they are at the top or the section failed to render

evidence_expected: The accrual schedule and its steps.
The service computation driving the current rate.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Read which of my records a legal hold covers
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172400 asks about their records' retention on 2026-08-11.
A legal hold covers a subset of them.
The hold's underlying matter is confidential.
story: As an employee, I want the suspended retention to be visible without the matter being disclosed, so that I can see why a disposal date is indeterminate
scenario: The worker asks when their records will be disposed of and some of them are held. Showing an indeterminate date with no explanation reads as a system fault. The held records show their retention as suspended by a hold, the hold's existence is disclosed and its matter is not, and the worker can see which records are affected without learning why.

acceptance_criteria.given: a hold covers some of the worker's records
acceptance_criteria.then: those records show their retention as suspended by a hold

acceptance_criteria.given: the hold's matter is confidential
acceptance_criteria.then: the hold's existence is disclosed and its matter is WITHHELD

acceptance_criteria.given: the hold is released
acceptance_criteria.then: the retention resumes and the computed disposal date appears

data_read.documents: the records, their retentions and any holds
data_read.compliance: the hold's existence, without its matter

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of which of their records are held and that retention is suspended.
The hold's underlying matter is WITHHELD from the worker entirely, including its category.

failure_modes.condition: the disposal date shows as indeterminate with no reason
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker reads it as a system fault

failure_modes.condition: the hold's matter is disclosed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a confidential matter is disclosed through a retention view

evidence_expected: The held records and their suspended retention.
The hold's existence without its matter.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Check the effective date of an entitlement I was granted
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172410 was granted an entitlement on 2026-04-06.
It became effective in the target system on 2026-04-08.
They could not use it until then.
story: As an employee, I want the grant date and the effective date to be shown separately, so that I can tell whether a delay was in the grant or in the provisioning
scenario: The grant was made on the sixth and the target system reflected it on the eighth. A single date hides which of the two took two days, and the answer decides whether the next escalation goes to the approver or to the connector's owner.

acceptance_criteria.given: a grant and its effect differ in date
acceptance_criteria.then: both dates are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: the effect has not occurred
acceptance_criteria.then: the entitlement shows as granted and not yet effective rather than as active

acceptance_criteria.given: the effect fails
acceptance_criteria.then: the failure and its retry state are shown rather than the grant appearing complete

data_read.identity: the grant, its dispatch and the target's confirmation

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of both dates and any failure.
The target system's operational detail is DENIED to the worker beyond the confirmation state.

failure_modes.condition: one date is shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: nobody can tell whether the approver or the connector took two days

failure_modes.condition: a granted-but-not-effective entitlement shows as active
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker tries to use it and reports a fault

evidence_expected: The grant with its date.
The target confirmation with its date.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Look up the source of a figure in a compliance report
preconditions: Tenant acme. A compliance report cites 1,802 workers in scope on 2026-09-30.
The figure derives from a population rule.
The rule's snapshot was taken 2026-09-30T23:00.
story: As an auditor, I want the figure to identify the snapshot it came from rather than the rule, so that I can reproduce the number rather than re-running a rule that has moved
scenario: A figure citing a rule invites the auditor to re-run it and get a different answer, because the population has moved since. The figure cites the snapshot with its timestamp, which is reproducible, and the rule is available as the snapshot's own provenance.

acceptance_criteria.given: a report figure derives from a population
acceptance_criteria.then: it cites the snapshot with its timestamp rather than the rule

acceptance_criteria.given: the auditor reproduces the figure
acceptance_criteria.then: they get the same number

acceptance_criteria.given: the rule is examined
acceptance_criteria.when: it is resolved from the snapshot
acceptance_criteria.then: the rule version that produced the snapshot is identified rather than the current one

data_read.population: the snapshot, its timestamp and the rule version
data_read.compliance: the report and its citation

authorization_and_disclosure: The auditor receives FULL disclosure of the snapshot, its timestamp and its rule version.
The snapshot's individual membership is DENIED to this citation, which returns the count and its provenance.

failure_modes.condition: the figure cites the rule
failure_modes.expected_refusal: re-running it gives a different answer and the report looks wrong

failure_modes.condition: the rule version is not recorded on the snapshot
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the snapshot is reproducible and unexplainable

evidence_expected: The snapshot with its timestamp.
The rule version that produced it.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: See whether a document requires a witness
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme UK Ltd. A deed requires a witness to the signature.
An ordinary agreement does not.
Worker W-172420 has one of each awaiting signature.
story: As an employee, I want the witness requirement to be stated before I sign rather than at rejection, so that I arrange a witness before I sit down to sign
scenario: One document needs a witness and one does not, and a worker who signs both alone has one rejected. The requirement is stated on the document before signing, with what the witness must do and who may act as one, so the arrangement happens before rather than after.

acceptance_criteria.given: a document requires a witness
acceptance_criteria.then: the requirement, the witness's role and the eligibility criteria are stated before signing

acceptance_criteria.given: a document does not require one
acceptance_criteria.then: that is stated rather than being an absence

acceptance_criteria.given: a document is signed without a required witness
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with the requirement named rather than being accepted and challenged later

data_read.documents: the documents, their execution requirements and the witness criteria

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the execution requirements before signing.
The counterparty's own execution arrangements are DENIED to the worker where the document is separately executed.

failure_modes.condition: the requirement appears at rejection
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker signs alone and has to sign again

failure_modes.condition: the absence of a requirement is not stated
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker arranges a witness for a document that does not need one

evidence_expected: The execution requirements as presented.
The witness eligibility criteria.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Check which of my time entries a manager changed
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172430's timecard for the period ending 2026-05-15 was adjusted by their manager.
Two entries changed and one was added.
The worker submitted the original.
story: As an employee, I want the changes to be attributed and comparable against what I submitted, so that I can see what changed rather than only what stands
scenario: The manager changed two entries and added one, and the approved timecard shows only the result. A worker comparing their memory against the approved card finds a discrepancy with no explanation. The submitted version and the approved version are both readable with the differences attributed to the manager.

acceptance_criteria.given: a manager adjusts a submitted timecard
acceptance_criteria.then: the submitted and approved versions are both readable with the differences attributed

acceptance_criteria.given: an entry was added
acceptance_criteria.then: the addition is shown as an addition rather than appearing in the submitted version

acceptance_criteria.given: a change reduces paid hours
acceptance_criteria.then: the reduction is visible with its actor and any reason recorded with it

data_read.time: the submitted and approved timecard versions and their differences

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of both versions and the attributed differences.
The manager's private notes not attached to the adjustment are DENIED to the worker.

failure_modes.condition: only the approved version is readable
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker finds a discrepancy with no explanation

failure_modes.condition: changes are not attributed
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker cannot tell a manager's adjustment from their own error

evidence_expected: Both timecard versions.
The attributed differences.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Read which plan a deduction on my payslip belongs to
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172440's payslip shows four benefit deductions.
Two are for the same plan at different coverage levels across the year.
One is an employee contribution and one is post-tax.
story: As an employee, I want each deduction to name its plan, its coverage level and its tax treatment, so that I can reconcile my payslip against my elections
scenario: Four deductions and a worker trying to reconcile them against four elections. Naming the plan, the coverage level and the tax treatment on each turns a reconciliation into a comparison, and the two deductions for the same plan at different levels stop looking like a duplicate.

acceptance_criteria.given: deductions exist for several plans
acceptance_criteria.then: each names its plan, its coverage level and its tax treatment

acceptance_criteria.given: two deductions relate to the same plan
acceptance_criteria.then: their periods and coverage levels distinguish them rather than appearing as a duplicate

acceptance_criteria.given: a deduction is post-tax
acceptance_criteria.then: its treatment is stated rather than being inferable only from the order of the lines

data_read.payroll: the deductions, their plans and their treatments
data_read.benefits: the elections and their coverage levels

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of their own deductions and their attributes.
The employer's own contribution to each plan is disclosed where the tenant publishes it and is DENIED otherwise by name.

failure_modes.condition: deductions carry plan codes only
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker cannot reconcile a payslip against elections

failure_modes.condition: two deductions for one plan look identical
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a legitimate mid-year change reads as a duplicate charge

evidence_expected: The deductions with their plans, levels and treatments.
The elections they derive from.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: See the escalation path for a case I raised
preconditions: Tenant acme. Case HR-6310 is at tier 2 on 2026-06-15.
The path has three tiers.
The requester is dissatisfied with the handling.
story: As an employee, I want the path and the current position to be visible so I can ask for escalation, so that I know that a next step exists and how to reach it
scenario: A requester who does not know an escalation path exists concludes the answer they have is final. The path shows three tiers, the current position and the route to request escalation, which is a request rather than an automatic move because escalation on demand would empty the first tier.

acceptance_criteria.given: a case is at a tier
acceptance_criteria.then: the full path and the current position are shown

acceptance_criteria.then: it is a request with a stated basis rather than an automatic move

acceptance_criteria.given: the case escalates
acceptance_criteria.then: the new tier and the reason are shown and the prior tier's handling remains readable

data_read.case: the case, its tier and the escalation path

authorization_and_disclosure: The requester receives FULL disclosure of the path, the current tier and the escalation route.
The tiers' internal staffing and workload are DENIED to the requester.

failure_modes.condition: the path is not shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the requester concludes the answer they have is final

failure_modes.condition: escalation is automatic on request
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the first tier empties and every case is handled at the top

The escalation route and its basis requirement.

acceptance_criteria.given: a template is inspected before request
acceptance_criteria.then: the entitlements it grants and any conditions attached to them are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: an entitlement carries a training requirement

acceptance_criteria.given: the template changes
acceptance_criteria.then: it cites the template version it requested

data_read.identity: the template, its entitlements and their conditions
data_read.learning: the training requirements attached to the entitlements

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the template's entitlements and conditions.

failure_modes.condition: the entitlements are visible only after approval
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker requests a name and discovers what it means afterwards

failure_modes.condition: training conditions are not shown
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker is granted a role they cannot use until they complete a course nobody mentioned

The training requirements and their durations.
Zero-effect receipt.

title: Handle a document that must be executed by a date the signer is unavailable for
preconditions: Tenant acme. A document must be executed by 2026-07-31 for a statutory reason.
The required signer is on approved leave from 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-14.
No alternate signer is configured.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the gap to be surfaced when the deadline is set rather than at the deadline, so that an alternate is arranged while there is time
scenario: The deadline and the absence are both known now and the conflict is discoverable now. Discovering it on 2026-07-31 leaves no options. The signature requirement is evaluated against the signer's availability when the deadline is set, the gap is raised with both dates, and an alternate signer is arranged with the authority to execute rather than the document waiting for a return that comes two weeks late.

acceptance_criteria.given: a signature deadline falls inside the signer's absence
acceptance_criteria.then: the gap is raised with both dates rather than being discovered at the deadline

acceptance_criteria.given: an alternate signer is arranged
acceptance_criteria.then: it is verified before the deadline rather than assumed from their role

acceptance_criteria.given: no alternate can be arranged
acceptance_criteria.then: it escalates with the statutory consequence stated rather than the document simply being late

data_read.documents: the document, its execution requirement and its deadline
data_read.leave: the signer's approved absence
data_read.identity: the alternate signer's authority

data_written.documents: the raised gap and any alternate arrangement

authorization_and_disclosure: The alternate signer receives FULL disclosure of the document and the authority they are exercising.
The original signer's absence category is WITHHELD from the arrangement, which states availability rather than reason.

failure_modes.condition: the gap is discovered at the deadline
failure_modes.expected_refusal: there are no options left and the statutory deadline is missed

failure_modes.condition: an alternate signs without verified authority
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the execution is defective and the deadline is missed anyway

evidence_expected: The deadline and the absence dates.
The raised gap and the alternate's verified authority.
The escalation where no alternate exists.

title: Refuse an automation that would act on data it cannot read
preconditions: Tenant acme. An automation is designed to act on a compensation threshold on 2026-04-20.
Its service principal cannot read compensation.
The design assumes the read will be permitted at runtime.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the design to be validated against the principal's actual authority rather than assumed, so that the automation does not fail at 02:00 on its first run
scenario: The design reads compensation and the principal it runs as cannot. Discovering that at runtime means a failure at two in the morning and a design that has to change anyway.
