acceptance_criteria.given: a design reads a field its principal cannot access
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with the field and the principal named

acceptance_criteria.given: the entitlement is requested
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows its own approval path rather than being granted as part of publishing an automation

acceptance_criteria.given: the design is narrowed to avoid the field
acceptance_criteria.then: it succeeds and the validation is recorded as part of the published artifact

data_read.events: the automation design and its data access
data_read.identity: the service principal's authority
data_read.compensation: the field, not read

data_written.events: the refused publication and its named field

authorization_and_disclosure: The author receives FULL disclosure of the refusal and the unreadable field.
The compensation data itself is DENIED to the author and to the principal throughout, and the refusal names the field without any value.

failure_modes.condition: the design is published and fails at runtime
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the failure happens at two in the morning and the design has to change anyway

failure_modes.condition: the entitlement is granted as part of publishing
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an access grant is made by publishing an automation

evidence_expected: The design's data access per step.
The principal's authority evaluation.
The refusal with its named field.

title: Record a correction that the worker themselves reported
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172540 reports that their recorded start date is wrong on 2026-02-16.
The correct date is 2024-09-03 rather than 2024-09-30.
They provide their offer letter as evidence.
story: As an HR business partner, I want the worker's report and its evidence to be recorded alongside the correction, so that the record shows who noticed and what they showed
scenario: The worker noticed and produced evidence. Recording only the corrected date loses both facts, and a later question about why the date changed has no answer beyond an actor and a timestamp. acceptance_criteria.then: the report, the evidence reference and the verification are recorded with it

acceptance_criteria.given: the correction affects service-dependent entitlements
acceptance_criteria.then: the recomputation cites the corrected date and its evidence

acceptance_criteria.given: the evidence is held in a restricted class
acceptance_criteria.then: the evidence is referenced by digest rather than reproduced in the correction record

data_read.people: the start date revisions and the service computation
data_read.documents: the offer letter supplied as evidence

data_written.people: the corrected date with its report and evidence reference

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the correction, its evidence and any recomputed entitlements.
The reviewer's own verification notes are DENIED to the worker where they are internal; the verification's outcome is disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: only the corrected date is recorded
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a later question about the change has no answer beyond an actor and a timestamp

failure_modes.condition: the evidence is reproduced in the correction record
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a restricted document is copied into a record with a different access class

evidence_expected: The worker's report and its date.
The evidence reference by digest.
The verification and the corrected revision.

title: Handle an approval that arrives from a principal in another tenant
preconditions: Tenant acme. An approval is submitted for an acme proposal on 2026-09-14.
The submitting principal belongs to tenant borealis.
The principal holds an approver role in borealis.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the tenant boundary to refuse the approval before its authority is even considered, so that an approval comes from inside the tenant it decides for
scenario: A principal from another tenant is submitting an approval for an acme proposal. Whether they hold an approver role anywhere is a question the evaluation should never reach, because the tenant boundary comes first. acceptance_criteria.given: a principal from another tenant submits an approval

acceptance_criteria.given: the refusal is returned

acceptance_criteria.given: the attempt is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it appears in both tenants, because it is a fact about a borealis principal and an attempt against acme

data_read.workflow: the proposal and its approval requirement
data_read.identity: the submitting principal and its tenant binding

data_written.security: the refusal and the recorded attempt in both tenants

authorization_and_disclosure: The submitting principal receives the typed boundary refusal.
Whether the proposal exists is WITHHELD, and the refusal is identical for a real proposal and a fabricated identifier.

failure_modes.condition: the authority is evaluated first
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a question that should never be reached is asked, and the answer sometimes leaks

failure_modes.condition: the attempt is recorded in one tenant only
failure_modes.expected_refusal: one of the two parties never learns it happened

evidence_expected: The tenant boundary evaluation.
The uniform refusal.
The recorded attempt in both tenants.

title: Refuse a leave request that overlaps an already-approved one
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172550 has approved leave 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-14.
They submit a request for 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-18 on 2026-07-06.
The overlap is three days.
story: As an employee, I want the overlap to be named and the extension offered rather than the request being refused outright, so that I extend the leave I have rather than starting again
scenario: The worker almost certainly wants to extend rather than to book overlapping leave. Refusing outright makes them cancel and rebook, which loses the approval they already have. acceptance_criteria.given: a request overlaps an approved one

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker genuinely wants two separate absences

data_read.leave: the approved request, the new request and the balance

data_written.leave: the extension or the refused overlap

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of the overlap and the offered extension.
Colleagues' approved absences are DENIED to the worker beyond any coverage constraint they trigger.

failure_modes.condition: the request is refused outright
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker cancels and rebooks and loses an approval they already had

failure_modes.condition: the overlapping days are booked
failure_modes.expected_refusal: three days are double-counted against the balance

evidence_expected: Both requests and their overlap.
The offered extension and its approval.
The balance after the change.

title: Record a training assignment that a worker completed before it was assigned
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172560 completed a course on 2026-01-19.
A requirement assigning that course is created 2026-03-02.
The completion is within the requirement's validity period.
story: As an employee, I want the prior completion to satisfy the new requirement rather than the course being reassigned, so that I do not repeat a course I completed six weeks ago
scenario: The requirement is new and the completion is not. data_read.learning: the requirement, its validity period and the worker's completions

data_written.learning: the satisfied requirement with its completion date

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker repeats a course they finished six weeks earlier

failure_modes.condition: the satisfaction runs from the assignment

The prior completion and its date.
The satisfaction dated from the completion.

title: Correct a manager relationship that was never recorded
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172570 has had no recorded manager since 2025-06-01.

story: As an HR business partner, I want the backdated relationship to be recorded and the routed approvals identified, so that the decisions made by a default are examined rather than left standing
scenario: The relationship existed in fact and not in the record, and for ten months approvals routed to a divisional default that had no relationship with the worker. The approvals routed to the default are the more important half: each was made by somebody with no relationship to the subject, and they are identified and revalidated rather than left standing because the outcomes look reasonable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a relationship was never recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded from its actual start date rather than from the correction

acceptance_criteria.given: approvals routed to a default in the interval
acceptance_criteria.then: each is identified by its routing and revalidated by the correct manager

acceptance_criteria.given: a revalidation reaches a different outcome
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a correction with its own intent and the worker is told

acceptance_criteria.given: the divisional default was itself a legitimate fallback
acceptance_criteria.then: the fallback's own authority is assessed rather than the routing being assumed invalid

data_read.people: the relationship, its actual start and the recorded gap
data_read.workflow: the approvals routed to the default in the interval

data_written.workflow: the identified approvals and their revalidations

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of any decision that changes on revalidation.
The reason the relationship was never recorded is DENIED to the worker where it names another person's omission.

failure_modes.condition: only the relationship is recorded

failure_modes.condition: the fallback's authority is assumed invalid
failure_modes.expected_refusal: legitimate decisions are reopened for no reason

evidence_expected: The relationship with its actual start date.
The approvals identified by their routing.
The fallback authority assessment and the revalidations.

title: Handle a payroll where a statutory rate changes mid period
preconditions: Tenant acme. A state minimum wage rises effective 2026-07-01.
The pay period runs 2026-06-25 to 2026-07-08.

story: As a payroll administrator, I want the period to be computed at each rate for the days it governed, so that the days before and after the change are paid under their own rates
scenario: The period straddles the change and a single rate is wrong for one half of it. Applying the old rate underpays the July days; applying the new rate overpays the June days and misstates the employer's own position. The period is split at the change, each segment is computed at its own rate, and the pay statement shows both segments so the worker can check them.

acceptance_criteria.given: a statutory rate changes mid period

acceptance_criteria.then: both segments and their rates are shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker's hours fall entirely in one segment
acceptance_criteria.then: one rate applies and the split is not shown for them

acceptance_criteria.given: an overtime premium spans the split
acceptance_criteria.then: it is computed per segment, because the regular rate follows the wages actually payable in each

data_read.payroll: the period, the hours and the rate history
data_read.regulatory: the statutory rate change and its effective date

data_written.payroll: the split computation with both rates

authorization_and_disclosure: The worker receives FULL disclosure of both segments, their rates and the split date.
The employer's own exposure analysis is DENIED to the worker; their own computation is disclosed.

failure_modes.condition: one rate is applied to the whole period
failure_modes.expected_refusal: one half of the period is paid at a rate that did not govern it

failure_modes.condition: the overtime regular rate uses a blended figure
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the premium is wrong in both segments and neither is defensible

evidence_expected: The rate history and the split date.
The per-segment computation.
The statement showing both segments.

title: Apply a benefits eligibility rule to a worker with no hours history
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172580 starts 2026-09-14 in a variable-hour role.

acceptance_criteria.given: the worker transitions to the standard cycle
acceptance_criteria.then: the point at which the standard measurement first applies is computed rather than being the next cycle boundary

acceptance_criteria.then: the rule's own precedence for overlapping periods is applied and recorded

failure_modes.expected_refusal: the worker's stability period is truncated or extended by an assumption nobody computed

evidence_expected: The initial measurement period and its basis.
The derived stability period.
The computed transition to the standard cycle.

title: Reconcile a workflow instance that reports complete with an open task
preconditions: Tenant acme. Instance WI-9410 reports ExecutionState COMPLETED on 2026-08-24.
A task it created remains unclaimed in a queue.
The task's own state is OPEN.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the inconsistency to be detected rather than the instance's own state being trusted, so that we find the orphaned task rather than waiting for somebody to notice it
scenario: The instance says it finished and a task it created is still open, which means either the instance completed a step it should have waited on or the task was created outside the instance's own bookkeeping. Trusting the instance's state leaves an orphaned task in a queue nobody owns. A consistency check compares instance states against their tasks' states, the inconsistency is reported with both, and the instance's completion is treated as suspect rather than the task being closed to make the states agree.

acceptance_criteria.given: an instance reports complete with an open task
acceptance_criteria.then: the inconsistency is reported with both states rather than either being trusted

acceptance_criteria.given: the discrepancy is investigated
acceptance_criteria.then: a premature completion and an unbookkept task creation are distinguished, because the remedies differ

acceptance_criteria.given: the remedy is applied
acceptance_criteria.then: the instance's state is corrected or the task is reattached rather than the task being closed to make the states agree

acceptance_criteria.given: the check finds a pattern across instances
acceptance_criteria.then: it covers the definition or the runtime rather than the individual instances

data_read.workflow: the instance states, the task states and their relationships

data_written.workflow: the reported inconsistency and its remedy

failure_modes.condition: the instance's state is trusted
failure_modes.expected_refusal: an orphaned task sits in a queue nobody owns

failure_modes.condition: the task is closed to make the states agree
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the symptom is removed and the cause produces the next one

The remedy and any definition-level finding.

title: Handle a jurisdiction that requires data to be deleted while a hold requires retention
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme GmbH. A retention rule requires deletion of a record class after three years.

story: As a compliance officer, I want the conflict to be escalated with both obligations stated rather than resolved by whichever system runs first, so that the decision is made by people who can weigh it
scenario: Two obligations point in opposite directions and either the disposal job or the hold will win depending on which is evaluated first. That is not a decision. acceptance_criteria.given: a deletion obligation and a retention obligation cover the same records
acceptance_criteria.then: the conflict is detected and escalated with both obligations stated

acceptance_criteria.given: the decision is pending
acceptance_criteria.then: they are preserved, because preservation is reversible and deletion is not

acceptance_criteria.given: the decision is made
acceptance_criteria.then: it records both obligations, the reasoning and the jurisdictions consulted rather than only the outcome

acceptance_criteria.given: the hold is released
acceptance_criteria.then: the deletion runs and its delay is explicable from the recorded conflict

acceptance_criteria.given: the preservation itself becomes unlawful in one jurisdiction
acceptance_criteria.then: the reassessment is prompted rather than the original decision standing indefinitely

data_read.privacy: the deletion obligation, its basis and its deadline
data_read.compliance: the litigation hold and its scope
data_read.documents: the records covered by both

data_written.privacy: the detected conflict and the recorded decision
data_written.documents: the preserved records pending the decision

authorization_and_disclosure: Both jurisdictions' counsel receive FULL disclosure of both obligations and the records' scope.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: a conflict between two legal obligations is resolved by scheduling

failure_modes.condition: the records are deleted pending the decision
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the irreversible option is taken while the decision is still open

evidence_expected: Both obligations with their sources and deadlines.
The preservation pending the decision.
The recorded decision and its reasoning.

title: Apply a reduction in force selection that a protected characteristic correlates with
preconditions: Tenant acme selects 62 workers for reduction on 2027-02-16.

story: As a compliance officer, I want the disparity to be examined before the selections are actioned rather than after, so that a criterion that produces a disparity is examined while it can still be changed
scenario: The criteria are facially neutral and the outcome is not. Actioning the selections and analysing afterwards means the analysis is about something that already happened. acceptance_criteria.given: a selection shows a disparity
acceptance_criteria.then: it runs before the selections are actioned rather than afterwards

acceptance_criteria.given: a criterion contributes materially to the disparity

acceptance_criteria.given: an alternative achieves the same purpose with less disparity
acceptance_criteria.then: the revision is applied and its basis is recorded

acceptance_criteria.given: the analysis concludes that the criteria are justified
acceptance_criteria.then: the analysis and its reasoning are retained under privilege as the basis

acceptance_criteria.given: a selected worker's rating derives from a period a leave covered
acceptance_criteria.then: the rating's own basis is assessed rather than the rating being taken as an input

data_read.people: the selection population and the criteria applied
data_read.talent: the performance ratings and their bases
data_read.compliance: the adverse impact analysis and its methodology

data_written.compliance: the analysis, its conclusions and any revision to the selection

authorization_and_disclosure: The analysis and its conclusions are FULL to counsel and the compliance function and are privileged.
Individual workers' selection status is WITHHELD until the selections are actioned, and the analysis is DENIED to selected workers by name.

failure_modes.condition: the selections are actioned before the analysis
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the analysis is about something that already happened

failure_modes.condition: a rating covering a leave period is taken as an input
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a criterion that looks neutral carries an absence the law protects

evidence_expected: The criteria and the disparity measurement.

Any revision and its recorded basis.

title: Handle a benefits carrier insolvency mid plan year
preconditions: Tenant acme's dental carrier enters liquidation on 2026-08-14.
1,420 subscribers are enrolled.

story: As a benefits administrator, I want the coverage gap and the unpaid claims to be handled as two separate problems, so that workers get coverage and the claims are pursued separately

A replacement arrangement is put in place with its own effective date, the affected subscribers are told what is covered from when, and the unpaid claims are pursued as their own matter with the subscribers told what is being done and what they should not do, such as paying providers directly.

acceptance_criteria.given: a carrier becomes insolvent
acceptance_criteria.then: coverage restoration and unpaid claims are handled as separate problems with their own timescales

acceptance_criteria.given: replacement coverage is arranged
acceptance_criteria.then: the subscribers are told what is covered from when and what the gap period is

acceptance_criteria.given: claims are unpaid
acceptance_criteria.then: the guaranty or creditor route is identified and the subscribers are told what is being done

acceptance_criteria.given: a provider bills a subscriber directly for an unpaid claim
acceptance_criteria.then: they are told what to do and what not to do, because a payment made now may be unrecoverable

acceptance_criteria.given: accumulators are held by the insolvent carrier
acceptance_criteria.then: the accumulators are reconstructed from the tenant's own claims data, their ConsistencyState is recorded as reconstructed rather than confirmed, and nothing is requested from an entity in liquidation

data_read.benefits: the enrollments, the claims and the accumulators
data_read.finance: the unpaid claims and the guaranty mechanisms
data_read.integration: the carrier's records and their availability

data_written.benefits: the replacement coverage and the reconstructed accumulators
data_written.operations: the claims recovery matter

failure_modes.condition: coverage waits for the claims to be resolved
failure_modes.expected_refusal: 1,420 people are uncovered for months while two organizations settle money

failure_modes.condition: accumulators are requested from the insolvent carrier
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the reconstruction waits on an entity in liquidation

evidence_expected: The replacement coverage and its effective date.
The reconstructed accumulators and their basis.
The claims recovery route and the subscriber advice.

title: Reconstruct an approval chain after a role hierarchy was restructured
preconditions: Tenant acme restructured its role hierarchy on 2026-07-01.

story: As an auditor, I want the approvals to be explicable from their authority snapshots rather than from the current hierarchy, so that an approval remains explicable after the hierarchy that produced it is gone

acceptance_criteria.then: the authority snapshot taken at the decision explains it without the current hierarchy

acceptance_criteria.then: it records what the approver held rather than pointing at a role definition

acceptance_criteria.then: it is a separate dated fact so the audit can see why the names changed

acceptance_criteria.given: an approval has no snapshot

title: Apply a wage transparency obligation retroactively to open postings
preconditions: Tenant acme has 84 postings open on 2027-01-01 when a new range disclosure duty takes effect.
41 were published before the effective date without ranges.
The duty applies to postings that remain published.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the open postings to be brought into compliance rather than being treated as grandfathered, so that a posting that is live on the day the duty starts is a live posting
scenario: The duty applies to postings, and forty-one are still published without ranges on the day it takes effect. Treating them as grandfathered because they were published earlier reads the duty as applying to publication rather than to publication's continuation. The forty-one are updated with ranges from the bound bands or withdrawn, applications received before the effective date are unaffected, and the update is a republication with its own date rather than an edit that makes the posting look compliant from the start.

acceptance_criteria.given: a disclosure duty takes effect with postings already live

acceptance_criteria.then: it is withdrawn rather than remaining published without a range

acceptance_criteria.given: applications were received before the effective date
acceptance_criteria.then: they are unaffected, because the duty attaches to the posting rather than to the application

acceptance_criteria.given: a posting is open in several jurisdictions with different duties
acceptance_criteria.then: each jurisdiction's requirement is applied to its own rendering rather than the strictest being applied everywhere by default

failure_modes.condition: the update backdates compliance
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the record asserts that the posting carried a range when it did not

The ranges from the bound bands.
The withdrawals where an update was not possible.

title: A worker exports their own data at a volume no self-service use explains
preconditions: Tenant acme. Worker W-172590 makes 47 subject access requests over 2026-11.
Each is narrowly scoped and individually valid.
Together they cover most of the tenant's holdings about them and their team's shared records.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the pattern to be assessed without any individual request being refused for being one of many, so that a right exercised often is still a right
scenario: Each request is valid and the pattern is unusual. Refusing one because there have been forty-six others would be refusing a right on the basis of its exercise. The requests are answered, the pattern is assessed separately for whether any individual request is manifestly excessive on its own terms, and the third-party content in the shared records is assessed each time rather than becoming easier to disclose through repetition. The pattern is surfaced to compliance as a fact, not as a ground for refusal.

acceptance_criteria.given: the requests cumulatively reach third-party content
acceptance_criteria.then: the third-party balancing runs each time and does not weaken through repetition

acceptance_criteria.given: the pattern is surfaced
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recorded as a fact for compliance rather than as a ground for refusing the next request

acceptance_criteria.given: the requester's purpose is asked about
acceptance_criteria.then: purpose is not a condition of the right and asking is recorded rather than the answer conditioning the response

title: A configuration change is timed to land between a preview and an execution
preconditions: Tenant acme. An eligibility rule is previewed at 2026-12-08T09:00 showing 40 affected workers.
The rule's underlying decision table is edited at 09:14.
The rule is executed at 09:20 affecting 1,140.
story: As a compliance officer, I want the execution to bind the configuration the preview evaluated rather than the current one, so that the preview and the execution describe the same rule
scenario: The preview and the execution are six minutes apart and a table edit sits between them. Whatever the intent, a preview that does not bind its configuration is a preview of something else. The execution binds the configuration digest the preview evaluated, refuses when it differs, and names both digests. The edit is legitimate on its own terms and is not reversed; what is refused is executing under a configuration nobody previewed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a configuration changes between preview and execution
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused on the configuration digest mismatch and both digests are named

acceptance_criteria.given: the preview is re-run
acceptance_criteria.when: the new preview binds the current configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: the execution proceeds against it and the affected count is whatever the current configuration produces

acceptance_criteria.given: the edit is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: it is legitimate on its own terms and is not reversed; only the execution under it is refused

acceptance_criteria.given: the attempt is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it records both digests, the edit's actor and the execution's actor as separate facts

acceptance_criteria.given: the edit and the execution share an actor
acceptance_criteria.then: it is surfaced to compliance, because the same principal previewing, editing and executing within eleven minutes is worth distinguishing from two people's timing

data_read.configuration: the decision table, its versions and their digests
data_read.population: the preview result and the execution's evaluation
data_read.identity: the editing and executing principals

data_written.configuration: the refused execution and the recorded attempt

authorization_and_disclosure: The executor receives FULL disclosure of the refusal and both configuration digests.
The 1,100 additional workers the current configuration would reach are WITHHELD from the refusal, which names the count rather than the membership.

failure_modes.condition: the execution binds the rule rather than the configuration
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a preview describes one thing and an execution does another

failure_modes.condition: the edit is reversed as a remediation
failure_modes.expected_refusal: a legitimate change is undone to fix an execution that should simply be refused

evidence_expected: Both configuration digests and the preview's binding.
The refused execution.
The recorded attempt with both actors.

title: A departing administrator schedules a job to run after their access ends
preconditions: Tenant acme. An administrator's employment ends 2026-12-19.
On 2026-12-17 they schedule a job to run 2027-01-05 under a service principal.
The job deletes a set of audit records.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the scheduled job's authority to be evaluated at execution rather than at scheduling, so that a job does not outlive the authority that created it
scenario: The job is scheduled under a service principal and its creator will be gone when it runs. A job that carries its creator's authority forward executes on behalf of somebody who no longer holds it. The execution evaluates the scheduling principal's authority at run time as well as the service principal's, the job is refused because its creator's authority has ended, and jobs scheduled by a departing principal are surfaced during offboarding rather than being discovered when they run. The job's own effect, deleting audit records, is separately a finding.

acceptance_criteria.given: a job is scheduled by a principal whose authority later ends
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, because the scheduling principal's authority is evaluated at execution

acceptance_criteria.given: a principal departs
acceptance_criteria.then: jobs they scheduled with future run dates are surfaced rather than being discovered when they run

acceptance_criteria.given: the job's effect is examined
acceptance_criteria.then: a job deleting audit records scheduled by a departing administrator is a finding independent of whether it ran

acceptance_criteria.given: a legitimate job was scheduled by a departing principal
acceptance_criteria.then: it is reassigned to a current principal with its own authority rather than being cancelled by default

acceptance_criteria.given: the service principal's own authority would permit the deletion
acceptance_criteria.then: it is still refused, because the scheduling principal's authority is a separate condition rather than being substituted by the service principal's

data_read.identity: both principals' authority intervals
data_read.provenance: the audit records the job would delete

data_written.security: the recorded finding and the surfaced jobs

authorization_and_disclosure: Operations receives FULL disclosure of the refusal, both principals and the job's effect.
The departing administrator receives nothing, and whether the job was surfaced is WITHHELD from them.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: it executes on behalf of somebody who no longer holds it

failure_modes.condition: the service principal's authority substitutes
failure_modes.expected_refusal: any departing principal can schedule anything a service principal may do

evidence_expected: The job, its schedule and its scheduling principal.
Both authority intervals at execution.
The surfaced jobs at offboarding and the recorded finding.

title: A tenant's own data export is redirected by a changed destination
preconditions: Tenant acme requests a full data export on 2027-01-12.
The export's delivery destination is changed at 2027-01-13T02:00 to an address outside the tenant's declared set.
The change is made by a principal with export configuration authority.
story: As an IT or access administrator, I want the destination to be bound to the export's own authorization rather than being a mutable configuration, so that an approved export goes where it was approved to go
scenario: The export was authorized to a declared destination and the destination is now different. If the destination is mutable configuration, an approved export becomes a delivery to wherever the configuration points at the moment it runs. The destination is bound into the export's authorization: a change invalidates it and the export is refused rather than delivered. The attempt is recorded with both destinations, and because the new one is outside the tenant's declared set it is surfaced to security rather than treated as a configuration correction.

acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused, because the destination is bound into the authorization

acceptance_criteria.given: the new destination is outside the tenant's declared set
acceptance_criteria.then: it is surfaced to security rather than treated as a configuration correction

acceptance_criteria.given: the tenant genuinely wants a different destination
acceptance_criteria.then: the export is re-authorized to the new destination rather than the existing one being redirected

acceptance_criteria.given: the export had already begun delivering
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused and the in-flight delivery continues to the authorized destination

acceptance_criteria.given: the changing principal holds export configuration authority
acceptance_criteria.then: their authority does not extend to redirecting an authorized export, and the refusal says so

data_read.integration: the delivery state

data_written.security: the refused export and the recorded attempt with both destinations

authorization_and_disclosure: The tenant receives FULL disclosure of the refusal, both destinations and the changing principal.
The new destination's own identity beyond its address is WITHHELD pending the security investigation.

failure_modes.expected_refusal: an approved export delivers to wherever the configuration points when it runs

failure_modes.condition: export configuration authority extends to redirecting an authorized export
failure_modes.expected_refusal: the authorization is decided by whoever configures rather than by whoever approved

evidence_expected: The authorization with its bound destination.
The attempted change and both destinations.
The refusal and the surfaced attempt.

title: Handle a request to correct a performance rating the worker disputes
preconditions: Tenant acme, Acme Ireland Ltd. Worker W-172610 disputes their 2026 rating on 2027-02-16.
They assert it is inaccurate rather than merely unfair.
The rating is an opinion informed by recorded facts.
story: As an employee, I want the accuracy of the underlying facts to be assessed separately from the opinion drawn from them, so that a wrong fact is corrected even where an opinion stands
scenario: A rating is an opinion and the facts it rests on are not. A rectification right reaches inaccurate facts and does not convert an opinion into one the subject prefers. acceptance_criteria.then: it is assessed against the retention basis rather than being treated as a rectification

title: Close a tenant's account with obligations that outlive the relationship
preconditions: Tenant acme's contract ends 2027-06-30 after five years.
Fourteen obligations remain open, including two statutory record retentions running to 2030.

story: As a compliance officer, I want the obligations that outlive the contract to be identified and assigned before the account closes, so that an obligation running to 2030 has an owner after the relationship ends
scenario: The contract ends and fourteen obligations do not. Two of them run for three more years and belong to the tenant rather than to the platform, and two belong to the platform under its own processor obligations. Closing the account without assigning them leaves obligations with no owner and, in two cases, records scheduled for deletion that a retention requires. Each obligation is identified, its owner after the exit is determined, the deletion schedule is reconciled against the retentions, and the exit does not complete until every one of the fourteen has an owner and a route.
